Title: Mindef sets up integrity system to tackle misconduct and plug leakages
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Defence Ministry has launched an integrity complaints system and appointed integrity liaison officers to combat misconduct, financial leakages and abuse of power within the ministry and the armed forces.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the initiatives were part of broader efforts to strengthen governance, improve accountability and close loopholes that could expose the ministry and the armed forces to integrity breaches.
"The complaints system would serve as an official platform for submitting information and complaints concerning misconduct, financial leakages and weaknesses in integrity.
"The 34 officers, appointed from various divisions and departments, would ensure the ministry's integrity agenda was implemented comprehensively, including at the operational level," he said.
Speaking at the launch of the Ministry of Defence Integrity Day 2026 at Wisma Pertahanan today, Khaled said integrity was particularly important given the ministry's responsibility for managing public funds and strategic defence assets involving billions of ringgit.
"Every allocation must be managed properly, every procedure must be followed, every piece of information must be protected and every defence operation must be carried out with the utmost responsibility," he said.
He warned that financial leakages and abuse of power could weaken the organisation, reduce the effectiveness of resources and undermine defence readiness in the long term.
More importantly, he said, integrity breaches could erode public confidence and damage the reputation of both the ministry and the armed forces.
To address such risks, Khaled said the ministry had introduced improvements to its procurement governance, including the composition of its Procurement Board and related committees, as well as evaluation mechanisms in accordance with Finance Ministry requirements.
"Cooperation with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) would also continue through annual integrity advocacy, literacy and education programmes.
"At the armed forces level, strategic cooperation with the MACC was further strengthened through a Note of Cooperation signed between both institutions on Oct 19.
"The cooperation would enhance intelligence, investigation and information-sharing mechanisms to support efforts to prevent integrity breaches," he said.
However, Khaled stressed that integrity was not solely about preventing major offences such as corruption, embezzlement and abuse of power, but also required discipline in everyday conduct.
"Arriving late at work, failing to use working hours productively, neglecting assignments and deliberately shirking responsibilities as examples of practices that could erode integrity.
"For military personnel, this included failing to handle assets carefully or carrying out operations carelessly along the country's borders and waters simply because no superior officer was present to monitor them," he said.
Speaking to reporters after the event, Khaled said integrity also required individual self-discipline and personal accountability, despite being a shared responsibility across the ministry and armed forces.
He said events such as Integrity Day were important in renewing personnel's commitment and reminding them to uphold integrity collectively.
"Through events such as this, we seek to remind one another and ensure that integrity becomes a shared value that everyone upholds.
"Through initiatives such as this, we hope it will become a continuous effort," he said.
Khaled also cautioned that technological advancements, including artificial intelligence and social media, had created new integrity risks, such as unauthorised information sharing, data manipulation and the misuse of system access.
He said such practices could compromise information security and national defence interests, stressing that technological progress must not come at the expense of ethical considerations
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Nadma coordinates 159 NGOs for northeast monsoon response
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has coordinated 159 non-governmental organisations (NGOs) at national, state and district levels for the northeast monsoon, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who is also the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) chairman, said non-uniformed NGOs are coordinated by the Social Welfare Department.
"This is based on Nadma Directive No. 1 on the national disaster management policy and mechanism," he said.
Zahid was responding to a supplementary question from Wan Razali Wan Nor (PN-Kuantan) during Ministers' Question Time here.
Wan Razali had asked what coordination mechanism was in place to mobilise volunteers and NGOs in disaster management operations during the monsoon, as well as Nadma's operational allocation nationwide and for Pahang.
Zahid said NGO coordination is carried out at all levels, including organisations affiliated with political parties.
He urged MPs to set aside political differences when responding to the monsoon season.
"Let us set aside political differences on this matter, because floods do not know political colours.
"They (the public) are all people who must be helped by the government, by Nadma in particular, especially at the state, district and community levels," he said.

Title: Father wants transparent probe into son's death at boarding school
Article:
TAIPING: The father of a Form Three student found dead at a boarding school in Kuala Kangsar yesterday wants a transparent and comprehensive investigation into his son's death.
Mohd Idzwan Razali, 48, said the family would leave it to the authorities to determine what had happened.
"It must be transparent and comprehensive. That is my hope," he said when met at the Taiping Hospital Forensic Department here today.
Idzwan said he was informed of his son's death by the police and the school principal about 4pm yesterday.
He said his son, Muhammad Al Fatih Mohd Idzwan, had been studying at the school since Form One and was expected to remain there until Form Five.
"He was my third child out of five. Overall, he was a good boy," he said.
Idzwan said his son had returned home during the recent Deepavali break before going back to the hostel.
He said his family lived in Kuala Lumpur, while his wife's family home was in Kuala Pilah, Negri Sembilan.
"All my children stay in boarding schools except the youngest," he said.
Asked about his son's experience at the school, Idzwan said there had been nothing unusual.
"His schooling was normal. His hostel life was also like that of the other students," he said.
He said his son last contacted him via Telegram before the incident, sending messages about everyday matters, including whether he had eaten.
Idzwan said the school had explained the circumstances surrounding the incident to the family.
However, he said they would not make any assumptions until the investigation and post-mortem were completed.
"They have explained it, but it is still subject to the outcome of the investigation and post-mortem. So, I cannot make any assumptions," he said.
He added that his wife was still deeply saddened by their son's death.
Muhammad Al Fatih is expected to be buried in Juasseh, Kuala Pilah, subject to the completion of the post-mortem.
The Form Three student was
found dead
on the school grounds yesterday.
Several police vehicles were seen entering the school compound this evening, believed to be in connection with investigations into the incident.
Police have yet to issue an official statement or provide details surrounding the case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor extends Visit Johor Year to 2027 with RM24.75mil boost
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor has extended its Visit Johor Year campaign until Dec 31, 2027, with RM24.75 million allocated for 12 tourism initiatives to attract more visitors and boost local businesses.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the extension would sustain tourism momentum beyond this year, generate income opportunities for Johoreans and strengthen the state's tourism industry.
The largest allocation of RM7.4 million will go towards upgrading iconic destinations, including Laman Bakau Parit Kasim in Muar, Pantai Minyak Beku in Batu Pahat and Labis Hot Springs in Segamat.
Another RM3 million will fund the third phase of upgrading works at Johor Zoo, while RM2.7 million is allocated for museum and heritage gallery improvements.
In addition, RM2.6 million will go towards recreational facilities at forest eco-parks, RM2.5 million in incentives for tourism event organisers and RM1.3 million for Visit Johor 2027 promotions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia looking at RM2 billion defence procurement deal with France
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is looking at
defence procurements worth nearly RM2 billion
from France, involving four combat search and rescue (CSAR) helicopters and 36 howitzers, following the issuance of letters of intent during French President Emmanuel Macron's recent visit to Malaysia.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the helicopters were estimated to cost RM1.3 billion, while the howitzers were valued at slightly more than RM600 million.
"We signed several important instruments with France during the visit by its president, Emmanuel Macron, a few days ago. One of the key agreements concerns cooperation in developing the local defence industry.
"France has clearly expressed its willingness to help Malaysia develop its own capabilities in producing defence products and assets, potentially starting with components and other related areas.
"This includes developing expertise and enabling local maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) centres. It is an agreement that the country very much welcomes because we have not had such a clear and focused agreement with any other country before," Khaled said at a press conference after the ministry's Integrity Day today.
He said the proposed procurements would also create opportunities for local companies to participate in the supply of equipment and components, supporting the development of Malaysia's domestic defence industry.
"For instance, for the purchase of 105mm howitzers, France will identify local companies that can become suppliers for the production process and related requirements.
"This is a very good agreement, which we welcome, and it can serve as an example for other countries when we undertake future procurements," he said.
On the timeline of the procurement of the assets, Khaled said this would be determined through negotiations following the issuance of the letter of intent, adding that he hoped the talks would begin as soon as possible.
During Macron's visit on Tuesday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the French president witnessed the handover of an LOI from the Defence Ministry to Airbus Helicopters for the proposed acquisition of four CSAR helicopters under Phase 1 for the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF).
Separately, Khaled and French Defence Minister Catherine Vautrin witnessed the exchange of procurement documents at Wisma Perwira ATM, including an LOI to French-German defence group KNDS for the proposed acquisition of a 105mm light artillery gun system involving 36 gun components for local integration.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tuaran Hospital to add 200 beds, targets specialist status
Article:
TUARAN: A new clinical block with 200 additional beds will be built at Tuaran Hospital as part of upgrades toward achieving specialist hospital status under the 14th Malaysia Plan (14MP).
Tuaran member of parliament Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau said the Health Ministry outlined the upgrading plans in a written parliamentary reply to his recent oral question.
"The Health Ministry said the plan to upgrade Tuaran Hospital into a specialist hospital to meet the needs of residents in Tuaran and surrounding areas will involve adding beds, specialties, doctors, nurses, ambulance services and parking facilities, alongside project cost and timeline considerations," he said in a statement today.
The existing Tuaran Hospital, which is over three decades old and was officiated by then health minister Datuk Lee Kim Sai in 1994, serves more than 150,000 residents in Tuaran and neighbouring areas.
Madius said the hospital will undergo several phases of facility upgrades and capacity strengthening under 14MP.
Currently operating with 82 beds, the hospital's strengthening plan covers facility upgrades, expanded medical specialities, human resource reinforcement and ambulance services.
"Among the improvements is the upgrading of equipment and systems for the second operating theatre, approved under 12MP at a cost of RM4.14 million.
"In addition, the placement of a computed tomography (CT) scan machine has been approved with an allocation of RM5 million, expected to begin operating at the end of 2027," he said.
Madius said Tuaran Hospital currently offers permanent specialist services across four fields, involving five medical specialists.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singaporean charged with trafficking over 19kg of cannabis
Article:
IPOH: A Singaporean man was charged at the magistrate's court here with trafficking 19.04kg of cannabis at Sultan Azlan Shah Airport on Nov 8.
Chen Long allegedly committed the offence at 6.20am at Baggage Machine A at the airport's check-in counter.
The charge was read in Mandarin before magistrate Norizan Riduan.
According to the charge sheet, Chen is accused of trafficking an estimated 19,040 grammes of cannabis under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
If convicted, he faces the death penalty or life imprisonment and, if not sentenced to death, a minimum of 12 strokes of the rotan under Section 39B(2) of the same Act.
The court fixed Feb 26, 2027, for mention of the chemistry report.
No bail was offered.
Deputy public prosecutor Ainin Sofiya Azlaini prosecuted, while counsel Sivahnanthan Ragava represented the accused.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor doubles subsidised Jualan Kasih locations to 748
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor will more than double the number of subsidised grocery sales locations to 748 next year under a RM30 million allocation in Budget 2027.
The expansion, up from 336 locations currently, aims to help households cope with rising living costs.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the Jualan Kasih Johor programme, which began in 2023, will offer a basic necessities package for RM15.
The package comprises a whole chicken, a tray of eggs and two litres of cooking oil.

Title: PAC to begin Sabah Pan Borneo Highway probe next Wednesday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) will begin its investigation into Phase 1 of the Pan Borneo Highway Sabah next Wednesday, starting with witnesses from the Works Ministry and the Sabah Public Works Department.
PAC chairman Datuk Wira Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the committee would call those involved in managing and implementing the project, including officers who had served since it was first planned, to give evidence.
"The PAC will not compromise on any breach of financial procedures or elements of abuse of power, and will not let any responsible party escape accountability," she told a press conference at Parliament today.
The investigation follows findings on the project in the Auditor-General's Report Series 2/2026.
Mas Ermieyati said the committee held a 90-minute discussion yesterday with five Sabah member of parliaments.
They were Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal (Lahad Datu), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (Beluran), Datuk Seri Wilfred Madius Tangau (Tuaran), Datuk Siti Aminah Aching (Beaufort) and Isnaraissah Munirah Majilis (Kota Belud).
"They shared first-hand accounts of conditions at construction sites, the daily problems faced by the people and the danger to road users' lives caused by delays to the project," she said.
She said the discussion gave the committee a better understanding of the problems.
Mas Ermieyati said the committee would refer any findings of misconduct for enforcement action.
The Sabah Public Accounts Committee has also been invited to participate throughout the investigation.
The toll-free Pan Borneo Highway was envisioned as a major transport link connecting Sabah, Sarawak and Brunei. However, progress in the two East Malaysian states has diverged sharply more than a decade after its launch.
The Auditor-General's Report Series 2/2026 found that
88 per cent of Phase 1 in Sabah,
which spans 706km, remained incomplete after 11 years.
Only four of Sabah's 35 work packages had been completed. Of the remaining packages, nine were classified as sick projects, 13 were delayed and nine were ahead of schedule.
In contrast, Sarawak had completed 10 of its 11 work packages, with the remaining package, WP11, 99.9 per cent complete as at March 31.
Despite RM10.547 billion of the RM11.153 billion allocated for Sabah's highway project having been spent, it remains significantly behind schedule.
The completion deadline has since been
extended to 2030 due to weaknesses
in project planning.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Investment surge propels Malaysia's Q3 growth beyond forecasts: analysts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter of 2026, expanding 5.5 per cent as stronger investment, manufacturing activity and resilient exports offset a moderation in household spending, analysts said.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) Research and CIMB Treasury and Markets Research said growth exceeded the consensus forecast of 5.3 per cent, with services and construction anchoring expansion alongside stronger manufacturing activity.
Both research firms said the economy maintained its growth momentum despite moderating private consumption, as investment strengthened and export performance remained firm.
HLIB Research said growth was supported by sustained expansion in services and construction, stronger manufacturing activity and a rebound in agriculture.
Private investment and household spending continued to underpin domestic demand.
"On the demand front, private consumption remained the primary driver of growth, albeit moderating slightly to 4.3 per cent from 4.8 per cent in the second quarter of 2026.
"This is partly due to a high base effect from the very first rollout of the RM100 Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) cash aid in September last year," it said in a research note.
CIMB Research said domestic demand growth eased to 4.8 per cent in the third quarter from 5.1 per cent in the previous quarter, mainly reflecting slower private consumption.
Private consumption growth moderated to 4.3 per cent from 4.8 per cent previously, its slowest pace since the third quarter of 2024, partly due to a high base effect following the SARA cash aid distribution.
However, HLIB Research said gross fixed capital formation accelerated to 8.1 per cent from 4.6 per cent in the preceding quarter, reflecting stronger investment in machinery, equipment and infrastructure-related activities.
Machinery and equipment investment grew 12.7 per cent, while private investment accelerated to 9.4 per cent from 4.3 per cent previously, indicating stronger capital spending momentum.
On the external front, exports remained a key growth contributor, supported by strong demand for electrical and electronics (E&E) products amid continued global technology demand.
CIMB Research said exports grew 25.2 per cent, while net exports contributed 0.3 percentage points to headline GDP growth, as import growth also accelerated to 26.7 per cent.
"Manufacturing growth accelerated to 7.7 per cent, driven by stronger E&E growth of 16.5 per cent, while non-E&E manufacturing moderated to 3.5 per cent.
"Construction activity remained uneven, with growth in non-residential buildings accelerating to 16.7 per cent, while residential buildings slowed sharply to 0.2 per cent and specialised activities eased to 6.6 per cent," CIMB Research added.
HLIB Research said the E&E cluster remained a key driver of manufacturing performance, supported by robust domestic activity and export demand.
The services sector grew 5.8 per cent, supported by stronger finance and insurance, information (ICT), and communications technology, and business-related activities.
CIMB Research said finance and insurance expanded 5.1 per cent, while ICT grew 8.7 per cent, supported by expanding data centre activity.
"Wholesale and retail trade growth moderated to 4.3 per cent from 4.7 per cent in the previous quarter, reflecting softer retail trade and motor vehicle trade.
"Mining contracted 6.1 per cent, reflecting scheduled oil and gas maintenance, while agriculture rebounded by 1.4 per cent on recovering palm oil output," CIMB Research added.
Meanwhile, Malaysia's current account surplus narrowed to RM5.7 billion, or 1.0 per cent of gross national income, from RM10.8 billion, or 2.0 per cent, in the second quarter, as higher services and primary income deficits offset the improvement in the goods surplus.
CIMB Research revised its full-year GDP growth forecast to 5.5 per cent from 5.0 per cent, following the stronger-than-expected third-quarter performance.
HLIB Research maintained its 2027 GDP growth forecast at 4.7 per cent, citing emerging downside risks from the fluid US trade and investment policy environment, particularly the new US Interim Final Rule on advanced artificial intelligence chips.
"We expect the Malaysian economy to sustain its momentum heading into 2027, driven by firm export activity, particularly for semiconductor-related products, on the back of strong global tech demand," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man shot dead after opening fire at police in Ipoh
Article:
IPOH: A man was shot dead after opening fire at police during an early morning operation on Jalan Persiaran Lembah Perpaduan here today.
The incident occurred at 2.30am when a team from Bukit Aman and the Perak police headquarters was conducting crime prevention patrols targeting robbery cases in the area.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said police had attempted to stop a car driven by the suspect.
However, the man got out of the vehicle and fired several shots at the police personnel while attempting to flee.
"The police team was forced to return fire in self-defence until the threat at the scene was neutralised.
"The suspect was pronounced dead by medical personnel at 3.40am.
"A pistol was also found near the suspect," he said in a statement today.
Kumar said the case was being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code for attempted murder and Section 3 of the Firearms (Increased Penalties) Act 1971 for discharging a firearm with intent to cause death or injury.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US company NTEC signs US$100mil coal supply deal with TNB unit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: American energy and mining firm Navajo Transitional Energy Company (NTEC) has signed a three-year US$100 million (US$1=RM4.11) agreement to supply coal from its southern Montana mine to Tenaga Nasional Bhd's unit TNB Fuel Services Sdn Bhd, the White House announced on Wednesday.
This was part of the US' move to deepen its relationship with Malaysia further.
President Donald Trump opened new markets for American goods and created opportunities for US companies, Washington said in a statement on its website today.
It said Trump concluded a two-day visit to the Philippines for a State Visit and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Summit yesterday, as he continues to support American jobs and strengthen US diplomatic leadership in the Indo-Pacific region.
"President Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim also announced that a US consortium will develop a sovereign super intelligence (SI) cloud for the Malaysian government, facilitated through US-ASEAN SI SPARK," it said.
According to the statement, Trump also announced over $17 billion in commercial deals and strategic investments for US companies that will support American jobs, bolster regional security that protects the US from illicit activity, and support a free and open Indo-Pacific that economically benefits American companies, workers, and consumers.
Other regional developments included a proposed US$2 billion project involving US company Latitude Energy and Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara to improve the utilisation of Indonesia's coal resources using US technology, it said.
Meanwhile, the US and Thailand announced the substantial conclusion of a trade deal that, once signed, would eliminate tariffs on 99 per cent of goods and remove non-tariff barriers on various American exports.
On regional security, the US said it would provide US$400 million in foreign military financing to the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including through long-range weapons systems, command and control capabilities, critical infrastructure and multi-domain drones.
The initiative, which the White House said would support 1,500 American jobs, forms part of Washington's broader defence and security cooperation with Southeast Asian partners.
NTEC is owned by the Navajo Nation and supplies coal internationally, including to South Korea and Japan; it transports its exports by rail to Westshore Terminals in British Columbia, Canada, before shipping them to Asia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MT Global 168 ketamine smuggling case: Tanker owner arrested, Indonesian police confirm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Indonesian police said Malaysian authorities have arrested the owner of the MT Global 168 tanker, which was intercepted with 1.16 tonnes of ketamine on board.
Indonesian National Police (Polri) Narcotics Crime Director Brigadier General Kristian Parluhutan Siagian said Malaysian police had informed them of the arrest.
He said Malaysian authorities had earlier sought information related to the investigation, including telephone numbers, the identities of suspects and their links to the ketamine smuggling network.
"This afternoon, we received information from the Malaysian police that they had also arrested the ship's owner," he was quoted as saying by Indonesian news portal Kompas.com at a press conference at the police headquarters in South Jakarta yesterday.
Kristian said Malaysian authorities had found indications that the vessel had repeatedly changed names, allegedly to conceal its identity and involvement in illegal activities.
"Regarding ownership, they have informed us that the vessel keeps changing its name, which indicates that it is being used for illegal activities," he said.
However, he said Polri had yet to receive the identity of the arrested owner.
"We do not have the name or initials yet; they are the ones who made the arrest," he added.
The case came to light after authorities intercepted the tanker on Oct 20 in waters off Tanjung Balai Asahan, North Sumatra.
A search of the vessel uncovered 58 sacks containing 1,160kg of ketamine. Laboratory tests confirmed that the seized substance was ketamine hydrochloride (HCl).
Polri later identified a Taiwanese national, known only as YCY, as a suspect in the case.
He is believed to have acted as the vessel's manager and controlled the ketamine consignment.
Meanwhile, seven Indonesians initially detained in connection with the case have been released after investigations found that they were unaware of the drugs on board.
The seven were replacement crew members who claimed they had been hired to transport oil.
The New Straits Times has reached out to Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Hussein Omar Khan for comment.

Title: Job fulfilment trumps salary in keeping Malaysian workers loyal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Job fulfilment plays a bigger role than salary in determining whether Malaysian employees intend to stay with their employers, with 91 per cent of highly fulfilled workers planning to remain at their workplace compared with just six per cent of those who feel very unfulfilled.
The findings are from the Singapore and Malaysia Salary Guide Report 2027 by Omni HR, an Asia-Pacific human resources and payroll platform, in partnership with PAYGAP Asia.
The report found that while competitive pay contributes to employee retention, job fulfilment has a considerably stronger influence on workers' intention to stay.
The proportion of employees planning to remain with their employers rises from 47 per cent among those earning at least 20 per cent below their peers to 63 per cent among those earning at least 20 per cent above them.
However, the gap is significantly wider when measured against job fulfilment.
The report found that 75 per cent of highly fulfilled employees earning at or below their peers' salaries planned to stay, compared with only 25 per cent of unfulfilled employees earning above their peers.
It also highlighted the importance of career progression, with Malaysian employees seeing a median promotion-related salary increase of 14 per cent, 2.8 times the five per cent median increase for routine pay adjustments.
The report noted that salary progression between entry-level and senior positions was also steeper in Malaysia than in some other regional markets.
"An engineering director earns about six times the pay of an entry-level engineer, compared with about three times in Singapore for instance.
"In finance, a director earns about four times the pay of an associate in Malaysia and about 2.6 times in Singapore," the report detailed.
Meanwhile, 26 per cent of Malaysian employees had gone at least 12 months without a pay adjustment, rising to 36 per cent among those with more than a year of tenure.
Employees who had not received a pay change in at least a year were 2.5 times more likely to resign, according to the report.
Omni HR chief executive officer Brian Ip said while salary was often the first factor employees compared, whether they found their work rewarding and considered pay increases fair also carried significant weight in their decision to stay.
"Pay is the first thing employees compare, because it is easy to measure. Whether the work feels rewarding and whether a raise feels fair are harder to see, and the evidence shows they carry more weight in whether people plan to stay," he said.
The report recommended that employers incorporate job fulfilment into regular employee check-ins, alongside reviewing salary competitiveness and career progression.
It also suggested that employers track employees who had not received pay adjustments in the preceding 12 months to identify potential retention risks.
The report combines anonymised payroll and human resources records from more than 200 employers on Omni HR's platform across seven Asia-Pacific markets, alongside salary and employee sentiment submissions from professionals on PAYGAP Asia.

Title: MMA wants nationwide audit of hospital infrastructure after Sabah power failure
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) wants the Health Ministry to conduct an immediate nationwide audit of critical hospital infrastructure following a reported power failure during surgery at a Sabah hospital.
Its president, Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan, said the incident, if confirmed, was unacceptable and raised serious concerns over patient safety and the reliability of essential hospital systems.
"No patient should have to undergo surgery under such conditions, while doctors should not be forced to compromise patient care because of failures in essential hospital systems," he said in a statement today.
He said reports of recurring air-conditioning breakdowns, electricity and water supply disruptions, and failures of backup power systems were particularly alarming.
"These are not minor maintenance issues. They can directly affect patient safety, infection control and the delivery of timely medical care," he said.
Dr Sivanaesan said the ministry should investigate the reports and conduct an urgent nationwide audit, particularly of operating theatres, intensive care units and delivery rooms.
Hospitals experiencing such failures should be prioritised for immediate remedial action, he added.
"Patient safety cannot depend on the resourcefulness of doctors working around failing infrastructure," he said.
He said healthcare professionals must be provided with safe and reliable facilities to deliver the standard of care expected by Malaysians.
A doctor at a Sabah hospital was previously reported to have used a mobile phone flashlight to stitch up a patient after a power outage interrupted a routine operation in the obstetrics and gynaecology department.
Zahir Hassan (PH-Wangsa Maju) told the Dewan Rakyat on Nov 17 that the incident was compounded by the absence of a functioning uninterruptible power supply (UPS).
He also highlighted recurring breakdowns of the hospital's operating theatre air-conditioning system and disruptions to electricity and water supply, which had affected operations.

Title: Transport costs push Malaysia's inflation higher to 1.9pct in October
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation edged up to 1.9 per cent in October from 1.8 per cent in September, driven mainly by higher transport costs and electricity, gas and fuel prices.
The Statistics Department said the transport group recorded the sharpest increase, with inflation rising to 4.2 per cent from 2.5 per cent the previous month.
The increase was largely driven by the cost of operating personal transport, which rose 4.9 per cent compared with 2.7 per cent in September.
The department said the average market price of RON97 petrol increased to RM5.00 per litre in October from RM4.64 in September, while diesel rose to RM5.20 per litre from RM5.05.
The average market price of RON95 petrol also increased to RM4.52 per litre from RM4.16, compared with the subsidised price of RM1.99 per litre.
Inflation in the housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels group also accelerated to 1.9 per cent from 1.4 per cent, following a sharp increase in electricity, gas and fuel costs.
The subgroup recorded inflation of 4.7 per cent in October compared with just 0.1 per cent in September.
The department partly attributed the increase to the revision of the Automatic Fuel Adjustment rate for domestic electricity users in Peninsular Malaysia consuming more than 800 kilowatt hours (kWh).
Meanwhile, the food and beverages group, which carries the largest weight in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) at 29.8 per cent, recorded slower inflation of 1.7 per cent compared with 1.8 per cent in September.
Food prices at home remained unchanged at 1.2 per cent, while inflation for food consumed outside the home eased to 2.5 per cent from 2.6 per cent.
Other groups recording higher inflation included alcoholic beverages and tobacco, at 2.9 per cent, and furnishings and household equipment, at 0.5 per cent.
However, inflation in restaurant and accommodation services eased to 2.1 per cent from 2.2 per cent, while education moderated to 1.8 per cent from 2.1 per cent.
Personal care and miscellaneous goods and services recorded a sharper moderation, falling to 1.2 per cent from 2.8 per cent.
On a state level, seven states recorded inflation above the national rate of 1.9 per cent.
Negri Sembilan recorded the highest rate at 2.6 per cent, followed by Kedah at 2.5 per cent, Johor and Putrajaya at 2.3 per cent each, Pahang and Labuan at 2.2 per cent each, and Selangor at 2.1 per cent.
On a month-on-month basis, inflation rose 0.1 per cent in October, unchanged from September.
The CPI increased to 137.7 points in October from 135.1 points in the corresponding month last year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor, Singapore fund RM220k study to prepare locals for JS-SEZ jobs
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor and Singapore will jointly fund a RM220,000 study to identify skills demanded by employers in the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).
The initiative aims to help local training institutions prepare Johoreans for upcoming job opportunities.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said both sides would contribute RM110,000 each towards the Johor-Singapore Talent and Skill Gap Study.
He said the move followed the inaugural Johor-Singapore Joint Ministerial Committee for Cooperation meeting on Nov 2.
Approved JS-SEZ investments between Jan 2025 and June 2026 have the potential to generate 28,755 jobs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Cable theft disrupts services on busy northern rail route
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cable theft disrupted the signalling system along the Bukit Mertajam railway line today, causing delays of up to 80 minutes to Electric Train Service (ETS) and KTM Northern Sector services.
Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB), in a Facebook post, said the disruption was expected to cause delays of more than 60 minutes from the original train schedules.
"Following a signalling system disruption caused by cable theft along the Bukit Mertajam line, train services on this route are expected to experience delays of more than 60 minutes.
"Repair works are underway," it said.
Several ETS and KTM Komuter Utara services continued to experience delays.
Among ETS services, train 9323 recorded the longest delay at 46 minutes, followed by train 9123 (44 minutes), 9343 (37 minutes), 9223 (33 minutes) and 9425 (30 minutes).
KTM Komuter Utara services were more severely affected, with train 2809 recording an 80-minute delay, followed by train 2908 (70 minutes) and 2912 (63 minutes).
Other affected Komuter services included train 2815 (41 minutes), 2810 (23 minutes) and 2915 (16 minutes).
KTMB said repair works were being carried out to restore normal operations.
KTMB recorded 45 cable theft cases in the northern sector between January and May 2025, with losses since 2024 reaching RM1.44 million by March 2025.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motorcyclist swept away by floodwaters rescued after clinging to tree
Article:
BENTONG: A motorcyclist was
rescued after clinging to an oil palm tree
for safety when fast-moving floodwaters swept him off a flooded stretch of Jalan Telemong-Chemomoi near Karak yesterday.
The man, believed to be in his 40s, had been travelling alone from Chemomoi towards Telemong when he attempted to cross the inundated road and was swept into an oil palm plantation along with his motorcycle. Passers-by pulled him to safety using a steel cable at 8pm.
Pelangai assemblyman Datuk Amizar Abu Adam posted a one-minute-and-10-second video of the rescue on his Facebook page.
The footage showed two men wading through chest-deep floodwaters to reach the victim before throwing him a steel cable attached to a four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle parked nearby, as torrents of water rushed around him.
"It was a tense moment as the owners of several 4WD vehicles crossing the flooded stretch used a steel cable to reach the victim and pull him to safety before he was swept away further.
"The victim was eventually rescued," Amizar said in the caption accompanying the video.
Meanwhile, heavy rain yesterday caused flash floods in several low-lying residential areas and business premises in Karak town.
Several roads, including those in Taman Permai, Karak Avenue and Jalan Chemomoi in Pelangai, were inundated and impassable to light vehicles.
Videos and photographs of floodwaters surging across roads and inundating business premises circulated widely on social media, though the water has since receded in most affected areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor allocates RM9mil for Islamic programmes
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor will introduce a voluntary weekly fasting programme every Thursday next year to encourage sunnah practices, strengthen mosque activities and foster closer ties between leaders and the public.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said RM6 million had been allocated to strengthen the Semarak Maghrib and Isyak programme, which includes communal breaking of fast and Maghrib and Isyak prayers.
Another RM3 million will be allocated to continue Semarak Subuh Johor, which encourages congregational dawn prayers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: WhatsApp group misunderstanding leads to Form Two student beaten, three students detained
Article:
TANGKAK: A misunderstanding over messages in a WhatsApp group is believed to have led to a Form Two student being beaten up by three male students at a secondary school here.
In the incident at 8am on Nov 13, the victim was allegedly kicked and punched repeatedly in the classroom by the three 15-year-old students.
The incident came to light after a video of the assault went viral on social media.
Tangkak police chief Superintendent Mohd Roslan Talib said police received a report on the incident at 12.09am on Nov 14.
He said the victim sought treatment at the Sultanah Fatimah Specialist Hospital (HPSF) in Muar after sustaining injuries to several parts of his body.
"Medical examinations found the victim suffered injuries to his head, chest, abdomen and left arm.
"Acting on the report, police identified and arrested the three male students suspected of involvement in the incident.
"Initial investigations found the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding over a WhatsApp group chat, which sparked dissatisfaction among the students," he said in a statement.
Roslan said all three suspects admitted their involvement during questioning.
The case is being investigated under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt.
"Police view any bullying and violence, especially involving school students, seriously.
"Resorting to force to resolve misunderstandings not only causes injury, but also endangers the victim's safety.
"Parents and schools are urged to remain vigilant over their children's behaviour and social circles, and not take any bullying complaints lightly," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two men remanded over RM500,000 goldsmith shop robbery
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: Two men suspected of robbing a goldsmith shop in Batu Enam, Gong Badak, of jewellery worth RM500,000 have been remanded for seven days to assist police investigations.
Magistrate Nur Akmal Mohd Bakri issued the remand order today, allowing the suspects to be held from Nov 19 to 25.
The robbery took place at 10.45am on Nov 12, when the two men, wearing helmets and face coverings, entered the Permata Al-Idrus goldsmith shop.
One of the suspects, armed with a parang, entered the inner section of the shop while his accomplice kept watch and monitored the employees.
All employees fled to the back of the premises for safety.
The suspects then grabbed three trays of jewellery worth an estimated RM500,000 before fleeing in a white Perodua Axia.
The case is being investigated under Section 395 of the Penal Code for gang robbery, which carries a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and whipping, and Section 397 for armed robbery, which provides for imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor Budget 2027 allocates RM3bil for development, people's aid
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johoreans can expect more financial assistance, housing support and cost-of-living relief under the state's RM3.07 billion Budget 2027 tabled today.
Themed Johor Maju, Rakyat Sejahtera (Johor advances, people prosper), the budget outlines 284 commitments targeting B40 and M40 households, entrepreneurs, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), farmers and the agriculture sector.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said Johor will channel RM1.53 billion towards development projects next year, accounting for almost half of its total expenditure, to ensure economic growth translates into better living conditions.
"The allocation is part of the 284 commitments outlined under the six pillars of the Johor Maju framework in Budget 2027.
"Johor will also channel its growing revenue towards helping more vulnerable groups, including poor families, orphans, people with disabilities (PwDs) and senior citizens.
"The government I lead will continue to work wholeheartedly, serve and care for the people regardless of their political background, race or religion. We will serve everyone," he said when tabling the budget at the state assembly sitting at Dewan Persidangan, Bangunan Sultan Ismail, here today.
For 2027, Johor projected revenue of RM3.08 billion against expenditure of RM3.07 billion, resulting in an estimated surplus of RM2.33 million.
Onn Hafiz said state revenue had reached RM2.8 billion as of this morning, representing 110 per cent of the original estimate for 2026.
He said he was confident that Johor's revenue would surpass RM3 billion for the first time in the state's history by the end of this year.
"This is the Johor we want — economically advanced, prosperous and with a happy Bangsa Johor," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Airlines earns World's Best MICE Airline 2026 title
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines has strengthened its position in the aviation industry after being recognised internationally for its role in supporting the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) sector.
At the 2026 World MICE Awards, the national carrier won both the World's Best MICE Airline 2026 and Asia's Best MICE Airline 2026 titles.
The awards recognise its onboard travel experience and range of solutions tailored to the needs of event organisers.
Beyond its MICE services, Malaysia Airlines offers extensive destination connectivity, onboard comfort, dining options and flexible booking arrangements to cater to different travel needs.
SUPPORTING MICE TRAVEL
For organisers managing events involving delegates from different cities and countries, coordinating group travel can be challenging.
Through MHcorporate EVENTS, Malaysia Airlines offers a dedicated service to simplify travel arrangements.
This includes preferential fares, special group rates and the flexibility for delegates to travel up to seven days before and after an event, whether attending conferences or exhibitions.
The service also caters to specialised group movements, including concert tours, artists' entourages and festival-related events.
Organisers can also benefit from the airline's network of more than 70 destinations worldwide, complemented by sister airline Firefly's regional network.
This helps connect attendees from across Asia and beyond.
CONNECTIVITY ACROSS DESTINATIONS
With its extensive network, Malaysia Airlines connects passengers to destinations across different regions while helping organisers bring international delegates together.
Its connectivity through Firefly further expands travel options across the region, catering to both smaller groups and larger-scale movements.
COMFORT THROUGHOUT THE JOURNEY
Passengers travelling aboard Malaysia Airlines' A330neo can enjoy a range of onboard features designed to enhance comfort and convenience throughout their journey.
Business Class
• Fully flat beds for a more comfortable rest.
• Privacy doors and direct aisle access.
• 17.3-inch 4K entertainment screens.
• Built-in wireless charging.
Economy Class
• 13.3-inch 4K entertainment screens.
• Extra legroom in selected seats.
Passengers in both cabins can also enjoy complimentary unlimited Wi-Fi, allowing them to stay connected throughout their journey.
DINING WITH A LOCAL TOUCH
The onboard dining experience features a rotating menu of regional and destination-inspired dishes, offering passengers a selection of meals throughout their journey.
Business Class passengers on eligible flights can also use the Chef-on-Call service to pre-order selected signature dishes before departure.
GREATER FLEXIBILITY WHEN BOOKING
Travel plans do not always go as expected. Malaysia Airlines therefore offers booking options designed to give passengers greater flexibility.
These include:
• Easy refunds: Passengers whose visa applications are unsuccessful may be eligible for a refund, subject to applicable terms and conditions.
• MH Flex fares: These offer unlimited rebooking, subject to any applicable fare difference, as well as the option of travelling earlier on the same day, subject to availability. Passengers also enjoy priority check-in, boarding and baggage handling.
From supporting international MICE events to providing greater comfort, connectivity and booking flexibility, Malaysia Airlines offers a range of services to enhance the overall travel experience.
For more information on Malaysia Airlines' services and MHcorporate EVENTS, visit
the official Malaysia Airlines website.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia opens lower on lack of buying interest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Thursday as market sentiment remained fragile, with no strong buying commitments amid a mixed Wall Street session.
At 9.18am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) shed 6.92 points to 1,559.81 from Wednesday's close of 1,566.73.
The benchmark index opened 6.26 points lower at 1,560.47.
Market breadth was negative, with losers outnumbering gainers 243 to 159. A total of 245 counters were unchanged, while 2,175 remained untraded and 14 were suspended.
Turnover stood at 475.73 million units worth RM254.04 million.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the FBM KLCI slipped to around the 1,565 level as investors remained cautious.
"Market undertone is still fragile with no strong buying commitments. Nonetheless, we noticed there had been some net foreign inflows over the past two days," he told Bernama.
Among heavyweight stocks, Maybank and CIMB fell two sen each to RM9.90 and RM7.01, respectively. Tenaga Nasional and IHH Healthcare slid four sen each to RM12.54 and RM7.88, respectively, while Public Bank rose one sen to RM4.51.
In active trade, BIG Caring Group and MYDCD gained one sen each to RM1.09 and 59 sen, respectively. CBH Engineering added 2.5 sen to 66 sen, MMAG Holdings went down half a sen to 1.5 sen, while Zetrix AI was flat at 5.5 sen.
Among the top gainers, Hong Leong Industries rose 64 sen to RM16.94, Dutch Lady added 50 sen to RM28.58, Cnergenz gained eight sen to RM1.13, QES Group inched up 6.5 sen to 64 sen and Cepatwawasan improved six sen to 79.5 sen.
Chin Teck Plantations led the decliners, falling 46 sen to RM9.74. United Plantations lost 34 sen to RM31.30, Malaysian Pacific Industries shed 24 sen to RM36.16, Kuala Lumpur Kepong shed 14 sen to RM20.66, while Sunway Construction Group fell 11 sen to RM7.43.
On the broader market, the FBM Emas Index fell 37.47 points to 11,566.73, the FBM Top 100 Index shed 38.60 points to 11,406.36, and the FBM ACE Index declined 4.04 points to 4,890.84.
The FBM Emas Shariah Index lost 47.68 points to 11,508.93, while the FBM Mid 70 Index slipped 5.60 points to 16,548.80.
Sector-wise, the Financial Services Index fell 31.27 points to 18,323.72, the Plantation Index sank 72.85 points to 8,657.42, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged down 1.45 points to 164.77, and the Energy Index declined 1.03 points to 768.10.

Title: UEM Sunrise earnings beat sparks analyst upgrades
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Analysts have raised their earnings forecasts for UEM Sunrise Bhd after the property developer posted stronger-than-expected third-quarter results, supported by higher joint venture contributions and improved property development earnings.
The group's net profit for the three months ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), surged 163.6 per cent to RM48.75 million from RM18.49 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 13.7 per cent to RM474.88 million.
The stronger performance prompted research firms to revise their earnings projections upwards, with analysts expecting the group to sustain its momentum into the final quarter, supported by higher contributions from joint ventures, property sales and land transactions.
Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) raised its FY26 earnings forecast by 22.9 per cent, mainly to account for higher contributions from joint ventures and associates, while Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) revised its FY26 to FY28 earnings estimates upwards by an average of 60 per cent after factoring in stronger sales and changes to billing assumptions.
CIMB Securities, meanwhile, raised its FY26 core profit forecast by 72 per cent to RM192 million, reflecting higher joint venture earnings and an estimated RM66 million net gain from the disposal of the Jalan Ampang land.
HLIB expects UEM Sunrise to record another strong quarter in Q4 FY26, supported by the recognition of the Jalan Ampang land sale, which it estimates could contribute about RM66 million in net gain.
The property developer has also surpassed its FY26 sales target of RM1.3 billion, securing RM1.94 billion in sales in the first nine months of the year, while its launches recorded a gross development value of RM2.64 billion, exceeding its FY26 launch target of RM2.2 billion.
The group's nine-month net profit rose 82.1 per cent to RM111.8 million, while revenue increased 11.8 per cent to RM1.43 billion, with stronger contributions from associates and joint ventures, particularly land sale transactions.
UEM Sunrise also declared a special dividend of 1.53 sen per share, which HLIB viewed as a positive surprise, supported by proceeds from the RM415 million Jalan Ampang land sale that strengthened its cash position.
Despite the earnings upgrades, analysts differed in their valuations of the stock, with HLIB maintaining a target price of 92 sen, PublicInvest at 60 sen, and CIMB at 72 sen.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call, citing progress in the group's development pipeline and land monetisation efforts, while PublicInvest reiterated "Trading Buy".
CIMB also maintained its "Buy" recommendation but lowered its target price to 72 sen from 83 sen, citing uncertainties surrounding US AI chip export restrictions that could delay industrial land monetisation, as well as the upcoming general election.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia's new vehicle sales climb 3pct to 673,412 units in 10 months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's vehicle sales rose three per cent to 673,412 units in the first 10 months of 2026, from 655,327 units a year earlier, despite a weaker performance in October.
The Malaysian Automotive Association (MAA) said total industry volume fell seven per cent year-on-year to 70,519 units in October, compared with 75,991 units in the same month last year.
Passenger vehicle sales declined seven per cent to 65,362 units, while commercial vehicle sales dropped nine per cent to 5,157 units.
However, sales improved 1.3 per cent month-on-month from 69,609 units in September, supported by a four per cent increase in passenger vehicle sales and an eight per cent rise in commercial vehicle sales.
MAA said demand for commercial vehicles had improved, with pick-up sales reaching 3,740 units, the highest monthly volume recorded so far this year.
It added that the government's support through the BUDI Diesel programme had also helped pave the way for a recovery in the commercial vehicle segment.
For the January-October period, passenger vehicle sales increased four per cent to 630,461 units from 606,443 units previously.
In contrast, commercial vehicle sales fell 12 per cent to 42,951 units from 48,884 units.
On the production front, total vehicle output rose three per cent year-on-year to 67,416 units in October.
This brings cumulative production for the first 10 months to 629,623 units, up two per cent from 617,693 units previously.
Passenger vehicle production increased three per cent to 63,598 units in October, while commercial vehicle output dropped five per cent to 3,818 units.
MAA expects sales momentum to continue into November, supported by a positive economic outlook and year-end promotional campaigns.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Myanmar's army-backed leader says he is reconsidering Asean ties
Article:
MYANMAR: Myanmar's military-backed leader Min Aung Hlaing said on Wednesday his administration was reconsidering the country's relationship with Southeast Asia's regional bloc Asean but would continue discussions with its members.
The former junta chief turned president, whose coup against an elected civilian government in 2021 triggered a nationwide civil war, also told parliament he planned to hold a peace conference in February, with the aim of ending fighting within his five-year term.
The state-run Global New Light of Myanmar newspaper reported on Thursday that the conference would be held in February 2028.
The position of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, which met this week without including Myanmar, appeared to disappoint Min Aung Hlaing, who has been pushing for re-engagement with the bloc.
Asean leaders said in a statement on Sunday that they may consider gradually restoring Myanmar's full political representation within the group if the country makes progress on their longstanding plan to resolve its crisis.
"They are imposing such pressure only on our country," Min Aung Hlaing said.
"There was never pressure placed on or indignity shown towards an Asean member before. But with Myanmar, they are doing that."
Since he became president in April following a widely criticised election dominated by an army-backed party, Min Aung Hlaing has visited several Asean member countries, including Thailand, Malaysia and Vietnam. Nearly half the bloc's 11 members have stepped up bilateral engagement since the election.
"For Myanmar and Asean to resume normal relations, we will take into consideration Myanmar's stance and the intentions of Asean member countries. We will continue to discuss with Asean member countries," he said.
The foreign ministry of the Philippines, the current Asean chair, did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Min Aung Hlaing's remarks.
Five-point consensus peace plan
At their annual summit held in Manila, Asean leaders said they had agreed to pursue a "calibrated engagement" through a "phased and progress-based" approach if Myanmar makes "sustained and concrete" progress on the bloc's proposed plan, known as the five-point consensus.
The five-point consensus, adopted soon after the 2021 coup, calls for an immediate end to violence there and the launch of constructive dialogue among all parties, while also offering Asean mediation and humanitarian assistance.
But fighting has raged on in Myanmar, where the military is locked in conflict with an array of armed groups. More than 100,000 people have died and millions have been displaced.
Despite calls for calm, the Myanmar military has stepped up a deadly bombing campaign in parts of the country, including multiple airstrikes that have killed large numbers of civilians.
Min Aung Hlaing offered few details about his proposed peace conference, which would be the first since he became president. Previous peace talk efforts have produced limited results.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Train shortage affects Kelana Jaya LRT frequency, says Rapid KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A shortage of operational trains on the Kelana Jaya LRT line is expected to result in longer waiting times and overcrowding on platforms, particularly during peak hours.
Rapid KL said its engineering team is working to increase the number of operational trains as soon as possible to restore service frequency on the line.
"Some trains will temporarily turn back at selected locations to help improve passenger movement and ease congestion at busier stations.
"Passengers are advised to allow extra time for their journeys and follow the latest updates through Rapid KL's official channels," it said in a statement.
Meanwhile, a review of comments on Rapid KL's official Facebook page found that many passengers had expressed dissatisfaction over service disruptions and unusually heavy congestion at several stations, particularly Jelatek LRT station.
Facebook user Muhd Syahmi questioned the decision to abruptly terminate train services at the station, claiming that there had been no apparent technical fault.
"Why did the train service stop at Jelatek? Nothing happened, there was no breakdown, but suddenly passengers were told to get off," he said.
Another user, CZ BC, described a frightening experience when the crowded train he was travelling on made an emergency stop after passing Jelatek station.
"After struggling through the crowd at Jelatek, the train made an emergency stop at Ampang while packed with passengers. I felt as though my arm would break from holding on to the handrail.
"Please, management, look into the current LRT service," the user said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: A six-minute train journey beneath the mountains: The ECRL Genting Tunnel engineering marvel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 19 — For passengers travelling on board the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL)، passing beneath the Titiwangsa Range between Gombak in Selangor and Bentong in Pahang may seem like just another part of the journey.

But beneath the mountains is one of the project’s greatest engineering achievements.

At 16.39 kilometres long، the twin-bore Genting Tunnel is not only a crucial link in the ECRL network but also showcases the engineering expertise، specialised technology and painstaking work required to carve a path through the rugged terrain of the Titiwangsa Range.

Today، the Genting Tunnel holds the distinction of being the longest rail tunnel in both Malaysia and South-east Asia.

“It takes approximately 6.2 minutes to traverse the entire tunnel at an average cruising speed of 160 kilometres per hour,” ECRL Head of Infrastructure Design Mohd Rahiman Ab Rahman told Malay Mail during a recent media familiarisation trip.

While passengers traverse the tunnel in just over six minutes، its construction presented a far greater challenge، particularly navigating the varying geological conditions beneath the 300-million-year-old Titiwangsa Range.

The giant that eats mountains

Because the terrain consists predominantly of hard granite، which causes significant wear and tear on heavy machinery، a custom-built، one-of-a-kind open-type hard-rock tunnel boring machine (TBM) was deployed to meet the challenging geological conditions.

Built by China Communications Construction Group in Shanghai، the machine measures 266 metres in length، has a boring diameter of 8.98 metres and weighs approximately 1,600 tonnes، tasked with boring through rock formations that have taken millions of years to form.

Moving at a maximum rate of 700 metres per month، the TBM excavated the tunnel، transported the excavated material to the surface and installed the concrete lining panels.

At the front of this rock-devouring machine، the cutterhead alone weighs approximately 900 tonnes، measures 25 metres in length and has a diameter of 8.98 metres which is the same size as the tunnel diameter.

The tunnelling work took approximately two years to complete، culminating in a major breakthrough on July 12,2025.

Mohd Rahiman said the Genting Tunnel was unique because it was excavated using a TBM rather than the open-cut method، given the significant overburden pressure exerted by the immense weight of rock and soil above the tunnel alignment.

He said passengers may not realise that as their train passes through the single-track tunnel، they are travelling beneath Genting Highlands، with as much as 750 metres of rock and earth separating them from the surface above.

To put 750 metres of overburden into perspective، it is equivalent to almost two KL Towers stacked on top of each other underground.

“Some of the early challenges involved dealing with water ingress — when external groundwater or surface water breaches the underground structure through rock fractures — as well as rock bursts (caused by the release of stored energy within the rock)، ” he said.

Inside the tunnel، Mohd Rahiman said emergency exits are provided at 450-metre intervals to allow passengers and crew to evacuate safely in an emergency، while the tunnel’s design also incorporates a Climate Change Factor (CCF)، with flood protection measures based on a 200-year return period.

“The technology used to make the Genting Tunnel possible is truly innovative and a marvel because China is far ahead when it comes to tunnel excavation.

“Ultimately، it comes down to combining Chinese technology with adaptations to suit Malaysian conditions، ” he said.

While passengers may not pay attention to their journey beneath the Titiwangsa Range، the Genting Tunnel’s significance to the ECRL is anything but hidden.

Title: PEOPLElogy’s leaders conference rallies corporate Malaysia to put people first in AI push, as ex-HRD Corp chief warns against cutting training
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 18 — Corporate Malaysia must keep investing in its people to get real
value from artificial intelligence (AI), Green Packet Bhd managing director and group chief
executive officer Datuk Shahul Hameed Shaik Dawood said as PEOPLElogy Berhad opened
its Build a Future Team (BAFT) Leaders Conference 2026 yesterday.

In his opening keynote, the former HRD Corp chief executive warned companies against
cutting training when business gets tough.

“The question should no longer be, ‘Can I afford to train my people?’ But rather, ‘Can I
afford not to?’ Technology can be bought. Capability has to be built,” he said in a media release. 

PEOPLElogy founder and managing director Allen Lee said: “Datuk Shahul has said what
every leader in this room needs to hear. AI will only be as good as the people we prepare to
use it, and that preparation cannot wait for better times. BAFT is where corporate Malaysia
commits to that work.”

Allen said leaders would be invited to make a Leaders Declaration, pledging to
keep people at the heart of their AI decisions and to help every team member take their first
step so that no one is left behind.

Welcoming delegates, PEOPLElogy Head of corporate planning Serene Tan, who heads the
organising committee, said last week’s I’m AI READY Summit showed that readiness was
about attitude, not technical skill.

“Being AI ready is not about being technical. It is about being willing. Willing to learn, willing
to ask, and willing to admit what we do not yet know,” she said in a statement.

“AI can make our organisations faster, but only people can decide what that speed is for.”

Now in its fourth year, the two-day conference at Marriott Petaling Jaya brings corporate
leaders and government together to plan their future teams around AI, under the theme
HumAnIze: Leading with Purpose in an AI Economy. Its sessions follow six pillars, Discover,
Design, Develop, Digitalize, Deploy and Declare, taking leaders from assessing where their
organisations stand to declaring their AI readiness.

Yesterday’s programme included the Leaders’ AI Competency Lab, an interactive workshop
where leaders worked towards a 90-day capability plan.

BAFT follows the three-day I’m AI READY Summit at The Campus Ampang, opened by
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo on Nov 12, where SMEs, students and workers took AI-
readiness assessments and received personalised upskilling roadmaps.

Speakers there urged Malaysians to use AI without losing the critical thinking employers
value most.

Former deputy international trade and industry minister Ong Kian Ming, an adjunct
professor at Taylor’s University, said he had taken on more than 200 interns over the past
decade, and those who stood out were proactive and added value.

He urged students to build a LinkedIn portfolio early but keep it personal. “It cannot be 100
per cent AI-generated. Having AI-generated components is not necessarily bad, but you
must use it creatively,” he said.

Pos Malaysia’s Natalia Navin said employers must be honest about AI’s impact on jobs. “I
won’t say to any employee that AI won’t take your job. AI can take over some tasks.
Employers must just be honest, and that is how you build trust,” she said.

Both events are part of National AI Readiness Week 2026 (NAIRW 2026), the flagship of
PEOPLElogy’s I’m AI READY movement, which aims to get 5 million Malaysians to declare
their AI readiness by 2030, in collaboration with MyDIGITAL Corporation.

The week closed today with the Asia AI Excellence Awards 2026 Gala Dinner,
recognising organisations setting the benchmark for responsible AI adoption.

Title: ‘This has never happened before’: Negeri Sembilan has no rulebook for a menteri besar who quits, says state secretary
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 18 — The Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office has yet to receive any official notification or letter from Datuk Ismail Lasim regarding his resignation as Menteri Besar.
State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said the office only learnt that Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, had stepped down through a statement on social media on November 16.

“This has never happened before (a Menteri Besar resigning), and we do not have any specific standard operating procedure on the matter (including whether the Menteri Besar is required to notify the State Secretary’s Office.”

“The procedure is different from that of the civil service, as it involves administrative matters governed by different processes from those applicable to civil servants,” he told reporters after attending the launch of the Aulad Sejahtera 2026 Module, which was also attended by Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, here today.

Negeri Sembilan Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir graced the event, which was also attended by Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud.

On the status of the Menteri Besar, Mohd Zafir said his office had yet to receive any latest information, including updates following Ismail’s meeting with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap here yesterday.

He said administrative operations at the State Secretary’s Office, Menteri Besar’s Office and state government departments continued as usual to ensure that public service delivery was not disrupted.

“The Menteri Besar’s Office is operating as usual, and its functions are continuing as normal. I have also not met the Menteri Besar (Ismail) so far,” he said, adding that he had been summoned to meet Tuanku Muhriz to discuss the latest developments.

On Monday, Ismail, 67, was reported to have resigned as Menteri Besar. He was sworn in as Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar on August 2.

The Negeri Sembilan Palace said that the resignation of the Menteri Besar would only take effect after receiving the consent of Tuanku Muhriz, in accordance with the provisions of the Negri Sembilan State Constitution.

Tuanku Muhriz was also reported to have granted an audience to Ismail following the political turmoil in the state. The meeting began at about 5 pm and ended at 6.30 pm. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal reserves decision on Penang tycoon Tan Kok Ping’s bid to overturn RM350,000 defamation award to Chow Kon Yeow
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 18 — The Court of Appeal today reserved its decision on businessman Tan Sri Tan Kok Ping’s appeal against a High Court ruling ordering him to pay RM350,000 in damages to Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow for defamation.

A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan, Datuk Aliza Sulaiman and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar reserved its decision after hearing submissions from Tan’s counsel, Datuk K. Kirubakaran, and Chow’s counsel, K. Simon Murali.

On December 3, 2024, the Penang High Court ordered Tan to pay RM350,000 in damages after finding that remarks he made at a press conference on October 18, 2023, were defamatory.

The remarks, made in Mandarin, were translated as “incompetent”, “ignorant” and “shameless”.
High Court judge Datuk Quay Chew Soon found that the remarks, which were published by six Chinese-language newspapers and an English-language daily, had seriously damaged Chow’s reputation.

In his submissions before the Court of Appeal today, Kirubakaran argued that the High Court judge had erred in law and fact in finding the three words defamatory.

He said Chow had merely stated the Malay translations of the three words as their alleged defamatory meanings in his statement of claim.

However, in his witness statement, Chow had expanded on the meanings, attributing to the remarks a more injurious defamatory meaning than that originally pleaded.

Kirubakaran argued that Chow could not rely on a more defamatory meaning than the one set out in his statement of claim, as doing so would be prejudicial to Tan.

He added that Chow should be bound by his pleadings.

He further submitted that the High Court judge had erred in accepting Chow’s self-serving explanation of the impugned remarks.

“There was an absence of evidence from members of the community or third parties or experts on Chinese language as to the meaning and effect of the impugned statement on Chow,” he said.

In response, Simon Murali urged the Court of Appeal to dismiss Tan’s appeal, submitting that the High Court’s judgment was beyond reproach and contained no appealable errors.

He further submitted that the High Court judge had correctly considered the relevant facts and applied the applicable legal principles in finding that Tan was motivated by malice in making the defamatory remarks.

Simon Murali said there was no appealable error in the High Court judge’s finding that Tan’s defence of justification was unsustainable.

He added that the High Court had also rightly rejected Tan’s defences of qualified privilege and fair comment.

Chow filed the defamation suit against Tan, who is the life honorary president of the Penang Chinese Chamber of Commerce, in January 2024 over remarks made by Tan concerning the sale of state land in Batu Kawan.

At today’s Court of Appeal proceedings, Chow was represented by lawyers Kek Boon Wei, Lee Wen Qian, Fatimatuz Zahra Suhaimi and S. Sharanya. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal reinstates 13-year jail term and caning for 64-year-old convicted of raping teen in Rompin four years ago
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 18 — The Court of Appeal today reinstated the 13-year jail sentence and four strokes of the cane imposed on an elderly man for raping a 19-year-old woman four years ago.

Justice Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, who sat with Datuk Ahmad Shahrir Mohd Salleh and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly, made the unanimous decision after allowing the prosecution’s appeal to set aside the Kuantan High Court’s decision to acquit Nasir Sharif, 64, the respondent.

“We are of the view that the 13-year imprisonment and four strokes of the cane fall within the permissible sentencing discretion.

“Accordingly, we order that a committal warrant be issued for the respondent to be imprisoned,” said Justice Ahmad Shahrir, who delivered the court’s decision today.

Justice Ahmad Shahrir said the Sessions Court judge had found that the victim, who was the second prosecution witness (SP2), was a credible witness, and that the High Court had made no finding that she was not credible.

“The legal principle is well established that the credibility of a witness falls within the purview of the trial judge, and we are satisfied that SP2’s testimony was credible and safe to rely upon,” he said.

Nasir was charged with raping a 19-year-old woman in a room at a house in Rompin, Pahang, at 3 pm on May 12, 2022, under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code.

The Kuantan Sessions Court on March 5, 2024, sentenced the man to 13 years in prison and four strokes of the cane after finding him guilty at the conclusion of the defence case.

However, the Kuantan High Court on January 13, 2026, acquitted Nasir after allowing his appeal against the Sessions Court’s decision.

The prosecution was represented by Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Aqilah Syaza Ariffin, while Nasir was represented by lawyer Mohammed Hissham Ramdzan. — Bernama

Title: Chips, batteries and optical tech: Anwar’s investment pitch in Shenzhen, Fastprint eyes PCB plant in Kulim
Article:
SHENZHEN, Nov 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met with representatives of China-linked technology and electronics manufacturing companies Fastprint and Fastrain here today to discuss developments and proposed investments in Malaysia.

The meetings were held on the sidelines of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) Economic Leaders’ Meeting.

Discussions focused on the semiconductor and advanced electronics industries, optical communications, as well as battery and energy storage technologies.

These sectors offer opportunities for Malaysia to strengthen its manufacturing and engineering capabilities while supporting the growth of the digital economy and the country’s energy transition, said the prime minister.

Anwar said the investments should bring direct benefits to the people through high-skilled job opportunities, technology transfers and greater participation by local companies in the supply chain.

“Cooperation with universities and technical and vocational education and training (TVET) institutions should also be strengthened to equip Malaysians with the expertise required by the industry,” he said.

Anwar said the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) and the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) would continue to follow up with the companies and relevant agencies to facilitate project implementation and ensure that investment commitments translate into industrial development and economic opportunities for the people.

Speaking to Malaysian reporters, Fastprint Group vice-president Stan Zhou said the company was looking into investing in a printed circuit board (PCB) plant at Kulim Hi-Tech Park.

Founded in 1999 and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, Fastprint is a global manufacturer of hardware and PCB prototypes and low-volume production, with operations in China and the United Kingdom.

Meanwhile, Fastrain is a global electronics and intelligent manufacturing company specialising in high-reliability components for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, high-speed optical modules, copper cables, automotive electronics and marine communication devices. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal says sentence too light, raises Arabic teacher’s jail term to 10 years for sexual assault of schoolgirl
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 18 — The Court of Appeal today increased an Arabic language teacher’s prison sentence from six to 10 years and ordered him to be caned twice for sexually assaulting an eight-year-old female pupil seven years ago.

A three-member panel chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, together with Datuk Ahmad Shahrir Mohd Salleh and Datuk Dean Wayne Daly, unanimously allowed the prosecution’s cross-appeal to enhance the sentence imposed on Ahnaf Afiq Shairul Bazri, 35.

“We set aside the sentence imposed by the High Court and substitute it with eight years’ imprisonment for the offence under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, and a further two years’ imprisonment under Section 16(1) of the same Act, together with two strokes of the cane.

“The court also orders the respondent to undergo counselling and police supervision for two years upon completion of his prison sentence,” said Justice Mohamed Zaini.

The panel dismissed Ahnaf Afiq’s appeal against his conviction and sentence imposed by the Muar High Court on March 11, 2026.

It further ordered that a warrant of committal be issued immediately for him to begin serving his sentence, while the bail money is to be refunded to his surety.
