In a brief judgment, Justice Mohamed Zaini said the court was not satisfied with the sentence imposed by the High Court, taking into account the gravity of the offences committed by the accused.

“The victim was only eight years old, and the accused had abused his position and the trust placed in him as a teacher entrusted with the care and education of pupils.

“These were significant aggravating factors.

“The accused also admitted to taking the victim into the room and closing the door.

“In the circumstances, we find that the conviction is safe and dismiss the appeal against conviction,” he said.

He said the victim, who testified as the second prosecution witness (SP2), had given clear and detailed evidence, which was further supported by her prompt disclosure to her mother (SP1) on the day of the incident.

“We do not consider the discrepancy concerning SP2’s position when SP4, the victim’s schoolmate, entered the room to be sufficiently material to undermine the credibility of her testimony,” he said.

On March 19, 2025, the Muar Sessions Court acquitted and discharged Ahnaf Afiq of the charges at the close of the defence case.

However, the Muar High Court subsequently allowed the prosecution’s appeal, set aside the acquittal, convicted the accused and imposed a sentence of four years’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane for the offence under Section 14(a).

The Court further imposed an additional sentence of two years’ imprisonment and two strokes of the cane for the offence under Section 16(1), to take effect consecutively upon completion of the sentence imposed under Section 14(a).

Ahnaf Afiq was charged with sexually assaulting an eight-year-old girl in the workroom of the library at a primary school in Muar, between 10.20 am and 11.20 am on October 3, 2019.

Deputy public prosecutor Mohamed Aznin Mohamed Ariff appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was represented by lawyers Mohd Radzi Yatiman and Nor Hafizah Abdullah. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak’s election fever rising: 517 forms sold, 10 days ahead of nomination day
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 18 — With 10 days to go before nomination day on November 28, preparations for the 13th Sarawak State Election are gathering pace, with 517 nomination forms sold as of yesterday.

Sarawak State Election Director Abang Noraffian Abang Ibrahim said sales of the forms, which began on November 6, included 390 purchased directly at the Sarawak State Election Office counter.

“The remaining 127 forms were sold through the offices of returning officers at state constituency level throughout the state,” he told Bernama when contacted here today.

Prior to this, the Election Commission (EC) said that all prospective candidates intending to contest in the Sarawak election were encouraged to pay their deposits early to ensure that the nomination process could be completed ahead of time and proceed smoothly.

The EC also reminded candidates that the nomination forms, which must be completed and checked by the returning officers’ offices, should be submitted by the candidates themselves, their proposers or seconders at the nomination centres on nomination day.

A total of 82 state seats are up for grabs in the Sarawak election.

On October 23, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg announced the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly, effective October 26, to pave the way for the 13th state election.

The EC has set December 8 for early voting and December 12 as polling day. — Bernama

Title: Unclothed man found dead at Pandan Jaya LRT carpark, police appeal for info
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The body of an unclothed, unidentified man was discovered in the carpark of the Pandan Jaya LRT station this morning.

Ampang Jaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid confirmed the discovery, The Star reported this evening.

“Initial checks at the scene found the unidentified man lying face down without any clothes,” he was quoted as saying.

A medical assistant from Hospital Ampang later confirmed that the man was dead.

The body has been taken to the hospital’s forensic department for a post-mortem to establish how he died, Khairul Anuar added.

Members of the public with information on the case are urged to call the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters at 03 4289 7222.

Title: Malaysian banks step up cybersecurity investment after recent attacks, says BNM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) is stepping up supervisory measures and regulatory requirements to ensure financial institutions remain resilient against evolving cyber threats, including their ability to detect, respond to and recover from cyber incidents, Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said.

He said financial institutions had also made significant investments to strengthen their cybersecurity defences following recent cyberattacks.

“As far as BNM is concerned, we place very strong emphasis on cybersecurity. We strengthen their resilience through supervisory measures and the ongoing enhancement of our Risk Management in Technology (RMiT).

“We also work closely with the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA) and financial institutions to strengthen the sector’s cyber preparedness, resilience and operational readiness,” he said at a press conference on third-quarter gross domestic product performance today.

Abdul Rasheed cautioned that as the country becomes increasingly digital and interconnected, financial institutions must be prepared for cyber incidents and even banking service disruptions, which could occur as part of everyday operations.

He said cybersecurity was a shared responsibility involving regulators, financial institutions and consumers, urging the public to remain vigilant against scams, impersonation attempts and other cyber threats.

He advised consumers to verify information received through social media, emails and other communication channels against trusted and official sources before sharing it or responding.

He also highlighted BNM’s “3S” approach — Soal, Sekat, Sebar (Ask, Block, Share) — as a simple reminder for the public to protect themselves against cyber threats. — Bernama

Title: Azalina demands explanation over leaked Najib Pardons Board minutes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has issued a statement calling on the relevant authorities to explain how the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting minutes that discussed Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon had been made public.

Speaking as Umno’s information chief, Azalina questioned if the minutes are officially declassified, when and by whom. The alleged copies of the meeting details are now being circulated on the internet, and first reported by news portal Malaysiakini.

All documents related to the Pardons Board are official secrets, and there are processes to observe before it can be made public. Umno’s statement referred to the DAP’s Tony Pua as the source of the leaked minutes.

“For documents with official secret status, the decision to declassify them must be made by the authority under Section 2C of the Official Secrets Act 1972 [Act 88] according to the applicable procedures,” said Azalina, who is also minister for law and institutional reforms.

Malaysiakini said it had received the minutes from a well-placed source and alleged that the documents were declassified for court purposes, in response to the Bar Council’s legal challenge against the house arrest order.

The documents do not appear to have been filed in court as of this morning, the portal noted.

Umno said the “responsible parties” must provide an official explanation regarding its declassification status, if they have been declassified, when and by whom.

Azalina also questioned the basis of authority and purpose of the purported declassification, and if circulating copies match the official record.

“What is the basis of authority used, the procedure followed, and the purpose of the declassification? Does the declassification cover the entirety of the minutes, including related attachments, or only certain parts?” The minister asked.

The alleged minutes detailed how FT Minister Hannah Yeoh and Attorney General Tan Sri Dusuki Mokhtar had opposed allowing Najib to serve the remaining jail sentence from his SRC International corruption conviction at home.

Malaysiakini claimed Yeoh was also reluctant to sign off on the meeting.

Najib is serving his prison sentence at home until August 2028 after he managed to pay the conditional RM50 million penalty.

Title: Too early to gauge impact of new US chip curbs on Malaysia, says BNM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The impact of the latest United States (US) restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres is still too early to assess, as developments surrounding the matter are still unfolding, said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour.

He said BNM concurred with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry’s (Miti) stance that Malaysia would continue to engage with the relevant authorities on the matter.

“This is one example where geo-economic risks are real and present, not just for us, but also for the rest of the world.

“As far as Malaysia is concerned, as Miti has also stated, we will continue to uphold rules-based trade, remain open for business, and pursue our diversification strategy,” he said at the release of the third-quarter 2026 (3Q 2026) gross domestic product (GDP) data today.

On Monday, the administration of US President Donald Trump issued a rule imposing new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres that enable Chinese companies to access advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips for training their AI models.

The reports also stated that companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil would be required to obtain US export licences for the most advanced chips, as part of efforts to prevent their illegal diversion.

Abdul Rasheed also emphasised that diversification remained a key strategy guiding Malaysia’s developments across various sectors, including date centres.

He noted that of the 120 data centre companies operating in Malaysia, only 17, or about 13 per cent, were Chinese-owned, while the remainder originated from the US, Australia, Canada, and Malaysia.

“This is where our investments (in data centres) are highly diversified. Therefore, the (US) restrictions are not expected to have a significant impact on data centre investments.

“Based on our estimates of ongoing and planned projects, investment momentum in data centres is expected to remain strong at least until 2028,” he said, adding that sustained underlying demand for data centres would also create lasting economic linkages for Malaysia.

According to Abdul Rasheed, the positive fundamentals are also consistent with the Malaysian Investment Development Authority’s (MIDA) approved information, communication and technology (ICT) investments, which increased to about RM38.9 billion in the first quarter of this year.

**Impact of US midterm elections**

Commenting on the US midterm election results, which could see the Democrats take control of Congress in January and increase scrutiny of the Trump administration’s tariff, data centre and AI policies, he said it was still too early to assess the potential implications for Malaysia’s economy as the situation continued to evolve.

He stressed that strengthening the country’s economic fundamentals and foundations would help shield Malaysia from global developments and uncertainties.

“On our part, we will continue to monitor the situation closely and assess its potential impact on the economy and financial markets, as well as the measures that we can put in place.

“In addition, this is where buffers matter. That is why I always stress the importance of building up buffers during good times, when we are (in a) strong (position), so that we can always draw on them during difficult periods or in the event of unexpected developments,” he added. — Bernama

Title: KPDN: No significant price hikes in essentials, public transport after targeted fuel subsidies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The implementation of targeted fuel subsidies has not resulted in a significant increase in the prices of essential goods or public transport fares, based on monitoring by the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN).

According to the ministry, the distribution of subsidies through the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) and Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) took into account their potential impact on the transportation costs of essential goods, land public transport fares, as well as ferry and passenger boat services.

“Based on monitoring of essential goods prices and public transport fares, no significant price increases have been reported following the implementation of targeted fuel subsidies, which began on June 10, 2024, for SKDS and September 30, 2025, for SKPS,” the ministry said in a written reply published on the official Parliament website.

The reply was in response to a question from Datuk Awang Hashim (PN-Pendang), who sought an assessment of the effectiveness of targeted fuel subsidies in addressing the operating costs of goods transportation and their impact on consumer prices.

He also asked about the intervention mechanisms that would be implemented should the government’s fiscal savings from the subsidies lead to higher prices for consumers.

KPDN said more than 850 Price Monitoring Officers (PPH) were deployed daily to collect price data from over 2,000 business premises nationwide. The data was analysed to detect unreasonable price fluctuations and serve as an early warning mechanism.

The ministry added that price information was also made available to consumers through the PriceCatcher application, enabling them to monitor prevailing market prices and make informed purchasing decisions.

It said targeted fuel subsidies for the transport sector also served as a government intervention to curb leakages and misappropriations, while mitigating the impact of rising transportation costs on the prices of goods.

KPDN said enforcement efforts had also been intensified to curb price manipulation and profiteering under the Price Control and Anti-Profiteering Act 2011 (Act 723).

These include stepped-up monitoring and inspections to ensure that targeted fuel subsidies are not used as a pretext to increase the prices of goods, while safeguarding consumer interests.

As part of its intervention measures, the ministry conducts a series of operations known as Ops Kesan whenever policy changes or economic developments could potentially affect the prices of goods and services.

“Up to 2026, six series of Ops Kesan have been conducted, including Ops Kesan 2.0 following the implementation of targeted diesel subsidies and Ops Kesan 6.0 to address the risk of profiteering arising from global cost pressures.

“Through these operations, KPDN monitors the entire supply chain and is empowered to issue written notices under Section 21 of Act 723 to examine changes in costs and profit margins. Legal action may be taken against parties found to have engaged in profiteering,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar credits govt measures for Malaysia’s strong growth despite West Asia crisis
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The Madani government’s proactive measures to safeguard economic stability and ensure fuel supply amid the West Asia crisis have helped Malaysia maintain strong economic growth despite external uncertainties, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

He emphasised that the government’s decisive action in addressing the West Asia crisis, supported by reforms implemented under the Madani Economy framework, has strengthened the country’s economic resilience.

“As a result, Malaysia has recorded one of the region’s strongest economic performances despite the various challenges facing the world,” said Anwar in a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance today.

He said the Madani government remained optimistic about the country’s economic prospects but stayed cautious about geopolitical tensions and climate-related risks weighing on the global economy as Malaysia heads into 2027.

Earlier, Bank Negara Malaysia announced that the country’s economy grew 5.5 per cent in the third quarter of 2026 (3Q 2026), bringing growth in the first nine months of the year to 5.6 per cent, up from 4.8 per cent in the same period last year.

Broad-based growth was supported by resilient domestic demand, which expanded by 4.8 per cent.

In September 2026, Malaysia recorded its highest monthly export value on record at RM215.1 billion, surpassing the RM200 billion mark for the first time.

Anwar said the government would build on previous Madani Budgets by raising the ceiling through stronger economic growth, higher investment and infrastructure development, while maintaining fiscal discipline.

“However, these achievements would mean little if we neglected efforts to raise the floor for the well-being of the wider population.

“Through Budget 2027, the Madani government is strengthening assistance, reducing individual income tax rates for eligible groups and improving public services,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PAC urges govt to break monopoly on vehicle supply concessions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has proposed that the concession for government vehicle supply be extended to other companies — categorised by vehicle type — to break the current monopoly held by a single concessionaire.

PAC chairperson Datuk Wira Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the categories that could be opened to other companies include vans, buses, four-wheel-drive vehicles, ambulances, and motorcycles.

This was one of three additional recommendations by the PAC to improve the management of government concession vehicles, following the tabling of PAC’s Follow-Up Action Report on the Management of Government Vehicles under Concession Agreements in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Mas Ermieyati added that the government must also finalise and enforce a supplementary agreement with Spanco Sdn Bhd to reduce vehicle leasing costs, as well as the excessive maintenance costs incurred when vehicles remain in use beyond their lease period.

She noted that the PAC’s investigation into the management of government vehicles — under a 15-year concession agreement 2 between the Finance Ministry (MOF) and Spanco — revealed weaknesses in contract management and governance practices. This has led to delays in replacing vehicles that had reached the end of their lease terms.

“The delay resulted in the government incurring additional costs for leasing and maintenance, while the imposition and collection of penalties for the delayed supply of vehicles were also slow.

“Overall, the PAC is satisfied with the follow-up actions taken by MOF in implementing the recommendations outlined by the PAC,” she said in a statement today.

The follow-up action report outlines MOF’s responses, along with PAC’s comments, regarding the actions taken on five key recommendations from the original report presented on July 9.

The PAC also proposed expanding the supply concession to include vehicles intended for critical and rugged use — such as ambulances — to ensure that essential vehicles remain consistently available and can be replaced promptly in the event of a breakdown or accident.

“The PAC further suggested that the government explore the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) to reduce reliance on fossil fuels, drive the development of the nation’s green technology industry, and attract foreign investment in this sector. This will support the national goal of becoming carbon-neutral by 2050.

“Furthermore, the PAC recommends continuous training for officers who manage vehicles within ministries and departments. It also calls on the government to prioritise data security and integrity when implementing the online system designed to manage and monitor concession vehicles,” she said.

The PAC has also requested the government to ensure the system is fully accessible and functional in rural and remote areas, including in Sabah and Sarawak, Mas Ermieyati added.

She said the PAC will continue to monitor the implementation of follow-up actions to ensure that the management of public funds adheres to the principles of transparency, accountability, and the best value for the people’s money. — Bernama

Title: Umno denounces leak of Najib pardon minutes as ‘provocation’, singles out Tony Pua
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Umno has condemned the circulation of purported Federal Territories Pardons Board minutes concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak's conditional pardon, denouncing the leak as a deliberate “provocation” to undermine the royal prerogative and demanding that Putrajaya clarify whether the Yang di-Pertuan Agong gave royal consent for their disclosure.

In a statement today, Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party viewed the dissemination of the confidential records with “deep regret” and treated the matter “seriously”.

He directed pointed criticism at former DAP lawmaker Tony Pua, who uploaded screenshots of the purported board minutes onto his personal Facebook account.

Asyraf stressed that the sovereign authority to remit, suspend, or commute criminal sentences remains the exclusive prerogative of the King under Article 42(1) of the Federal Constitution, insisting that all documentation originating from Pardons Board proceedings must be treated with utmost “care, confidentiality and respect”.

“The main question that needs to be answered is whether the declassification and dissemination of the minutes had the consent of His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong,” the statement said.

While acknowledging that the federal government is reviewing the declassification of the documents, Asyraf argued that any public disclosure directly touching upon proceedings presided over by the King requires prior royal assent.

He characterized the leak as “a form of insult and provocation” orchestrated to trigger partisan debate that demeans the monarch, accusing Pua of seeking to “appears to continually exploit” the sensitive clemency process “as political fodder” with disregard for the constitutional monarchy.

Demanding immediate transparency from the federal administration, Umno urged Putrajaya to detail the statutory basis of any declassification, identify which authority sanctioned the disclosure, and confirm whether the palace was formally consulted. Asyraf warned that if official protocols or secrecy laws were breached, enforcement agencies must take unyielding action to safeguard the sovereignty of the Malay Rulers and constitutional conventions.

The Umno statement conspicuously avoided addressing the substantive contents of the leaked document, which revealed that Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh formally opposed granting Najib a conditional pardon during the Sept 18 meeting.

The unverified minutes also recorded that the King was “inclined” to grant clemency, allowing the former prime minister to complete his custodial sentence at his residence after settling an RM50 million fine.

The political controversy erupts just days after Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail informed Parliament on Nov 12 that he would seek Cabinet approval to formally declassify the records, with Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil noting that ministers had requested legal counsel from the attorney-general.

The episode marks renewed friction over Pua's social media commentary on Najib's clemency, following a police probe in early 2024 when federal investigators summoned the former parliamentarian over posts criticising the initial royal reduction of Najib's sentence and fine.

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB to seek audience with Tuanku Muhriz as 10 sacked excos drop lawsuit
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 18 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ismail Lasim is scheduled to seek a fresh audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir this Friday to map out the state assembly calendar and explore solutions for 10 sacked executive council members.

A source said that the high-stakes consultation will mark their second royal engagement this week, following an audience granted yesterday at Istana Hinggap after Barisan Nasional (BN) publicly claimed that the Juasseh assemblyman had tendered his resignation, FMT reported.

“He will continue performing his duties as menteri besar as usual,” the source said, adding that Ismail and Tuanku Muhriz are expected to examine the potential reappointment of the 10 dismissed councillors to restore executive functionality and ensure the state administration can govern effectively.

“We hope that all parties would keep calm and pray for the best,” the source added.

The upcoming palace meeting follows an administrative standoff triggered on Monday when BN announced Ismail’s resignation as menteri besar.

The palace declined to act on the claim, confirming it had received an unverified letter delivered at midnight by a private law firm and reiterating that under the state constitution, the menteri besar must submit his resignation directly to the ruler, taking legal effect only with royal consent.

In a significant legal de-escalation earlier today, all 10 former exco members formally withdrew their lawsuit challenging Tuanku Muhriz’s decision to revoke their executive appointments.

The councillors, comprising eight BN and two Perikatan Nasional assemblymen, had their posts revoked in September after publicly claiming that Tuanku Muhriz was legitimately removed in April and declaring Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the state's new ruler, a move the royal household deemed completely incompatible with their sworn constitutional allegiance.

Title: Asean spoke with one voice to Trump on bloc’s common position, says Anwar
Article:
SHENZHEN, Nov 18 — Asean member states are committed to continuing to work closely together and upholding the centrality of the regional bloc, particularly through engagement with United States President Donald Trump, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

He said the consensus formed a common position conveyed to Trump during the Asean-United States Special Summit in Manila yesterday.

“We discussed the need for Asean to work together and present a common position to Trump, namely that Asean must continue to uphold its centrality and work together,” he said when met by Bernama after delivering a speech at the APEC 2026 CEO Summit here today.

He said this when asked to comment on the meeting between Asean member states and Trump.

Anwar also expressed his appreciation to the Philippine government and President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. for hosting and organising the meeting, which he described as having gone very well.

Elaborating on the outcome of the discussions, the Prime Minister said this session was far more substantive than previous ones, with the main focus directed towards strengthening the regional economy.

“It was more substantive, covering digitalisation, the economic framework, trade and intra-Asean trade,” he said.

The Philippines, as this year’s Asean Chair, hosted the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits from November 15 to 17, bringing together delegations from the 11-member regional bloc as well as its dialogue and sectoral dialogue partners.

This year’s edition was themed “Navigating Our Future, Together”. The chairmanship of the regional bloc has been handed over to Singapore for 2027. — Bernama

Title: No audience with Sultan: Perak MB office refutes viral state assembly dissolution claims
Article:
IPOH, Nov 18 — The Perak Menteri Besar’s Office has dismissed viral social media claims alleging that Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad had sought an audience with the Sultan of Perak to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly, describing the rumours as completely unfounded.

In an official statement today, the office refuted claims asserting that the Perak MB had met Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah to request royal assent for a snap dissolution, and that the monarch had consented to the dissolution of the legislature.

“The claim is not true and baseless,” it said.

The state administration revealed that it had detected manipulated graphics styled to mimic authentic television news broadcasts, alongside the recirculating of outdated news reports designed to sow public confusion over the legal status of the state assembly.

Saying that it views the spread of disinformation seriously, particularly narratives that misrepresent the royal institution and compromise state administration, the office confirmed that it has sought police intervention.

“In this regard, the administration has lodged a report with the authorities to enable an investigation and further action to be taken against those responsible,” it said.

The office urged the public to rely strictly on accredited government channels for factual announcements and refrain from circulating unauthenticated digital content across social messaging networks.

The denial arrives amid heightened national political speculation following Barisan Nasional's landslide victory in the Melaka state election over the weekend, which triggered fevered talk that the coalition could initiate snap dissolutions in states under its control to force an early general election.

Title: MCMC asks Anthropic to clarify report on Claude-powered voter targeting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Malaysia is seeking information from US artificial intelligence firm Anthropic over the alleged use of its technology in a political influence operation targeting Malaysian voters, the government has said.

Anthropic said in a report issued in September it had uncovered a suspected AI-powered campaign meant to disrupt elections in the Southeast Asian nation.

It pointed to an “overseas entity”, believed to have been based in Turkey, that abused Anthropic’s Claude AI model to generate around 1,000 fake accounts on social media platform X and create a synthetic news site.

“Based on the report, Anthropic alleged that Claude technology was used by an overseas entity to develop several components of the operation, including a targeting system, a network of fake social media accounts, fake news sites and related components,” the Malaysian communications ministry told parliament in a written statement on Tuesday, responding to a lawmaker’s questions about the matter.

The ministry said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission was “seeking further information and clarification from Anthropic regarding the report”, and would then “determine appropriate follow-up actions”.

According to Anthropic’s report, the entity “sold access to the platform as a paid influence-as-a-service capability”, marketing the infrastructure as “military-grade, AI-driven, real-time political operations ecosystem”.

“The operation involved the actors leveraging that platform built through Claude to profile and target voters in Malaysia, constituency by constituency, using census and electoral data that they had ingested,” the report said.

But the campaign was stopped “without evidence of breakout into authentic communities”, it said.

The report did not specify when the operation began or how long it lasted, but detailed Anthropic’s efforts to disrupt misuse of its AI models between December 2025 and August 2026.

The communications ministry said Malaysia was drafting a bill to “strengthen the country’s AI governance framework”.

“The government will continue to strengthen monitoring of the risks of misuse of AI technology as well as collaboration with technology providers, digital platforms and relevant agencies to address online harm and ensure that the country’s digital environment remains safe, transparent and trusted,” it said. — AFP

Title: MetMalaysia issues nationwide storm warning until 6pm ahead of evening rush hour
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a nationwide thunderstorm warning for this afternoon, forecasting torrential downpours, lightning, and gusty winds across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah, Sarawak, and Labuan until 6.00pm today.

The advisory, released at 3.20pm, blankets the entire states of Perlis and Kedah, alongside Seberang Perai Selatan in mainland Penang.

In Perak, stormy conditions are expected across seven districts, spanning Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Selama, Larut Matang, Kerian, Kinta, and Kampar. Along the east coast, the alert covers Jeli, Gua Musang, Tanah Merah, and Kuala Krai in Kelantan, as well as the highland and interior districts of Jerantut, Lipis, and Cameron Highlands in Pahang.

In the central and southern corridors, adverse weather spans the Klang Valley and southern industrial heartlands, blanketing eight Selangor districts: Gombak, Petaling, Hulu Langat, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Kuala Selangor, Klang, and Sabak Bernam.

The warning concurrently extends across the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, alongside Seremban, Rembau, and Port Dickson in Negeri Sembilan, the entirety of Melaka, and seven Johor districts including Kota Tinggi, Kluang, Kulai, Johor Bahru, Pontian, Mersing, and Segamat.

Across East Malaysia, the bulletin covers widespread divisions in Sarawak, including Kuching, Bau, Serian, Samarahan, Asajaya, Sri Aman, and Song in Kapit. The alert also spans central and northern Sarawak localities, encompassing Selangau in Sibu, Mukah, Dalat, Tatau, Bintulu, Subis in Miri, and Limbang.

In Sabah, squalls are expected across the Interior division covering Tenom, Beaufort, Sipitang, Kuala Penyu, Membakut, and Keningau, before moving along the West Coast across Papar, Penampang, Putatan, and Kota Kinabalu, with the offshore Federal Territory of Labuan also placed on alert.

MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings when satellite and radar indicators track rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour that is either imminent or projected to persist beyond an hour. The department noted that these advisories serve as short-term alerts with a maximum validity of six hours from the time of issuance.

Commuters and motorists heading into the peak evening rush hour have been urged to exercise caution on slick roadways, steer clear of open fields, and monitor official channels for real-time weather movements.

Title: Stay out of state affairs, Zahid tells Negeri Sembilan MB’s son after scapegoat claim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has warned the family of Datuk Seri Ismail Lasim against interfering in state affairs, after the Negeri Sembilan menteri besar’s son publicly questioned the coalition’s decision to announce his father’s purported resignation.

Zahid insisted that the leadership transition in Seremban remains strictly an executive and constitutional issue rather than a private domestic matter, according to Kosmo!

“This is a matter concerning the state administration. What does this family involvement have to do with anything? This is a matter concerning the menteri besar, not his father, Ismail Lasim,” Zahid said.

He made the remarks during a press conference after attending the 62nd Coordination Meeting No. 2 for 2026 between the Minister of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) and the State Executive Councillors for Rural Affairs (MEXCLUB), held at the Desaru Coast Conference Centre (DCCC) today.

The rebuke follows an Instagram post by Ismail’s son, Naim, who expressed dismay over the coalition’s handling of the announcement and suggested that his father was being turned into a political scapegoat.

The friction erupted after BN issued a statement on Monday declaring that Ismail had submitted his resignation as menteri besar.

However, the premature announcement triggered an administrative impasse after the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, reportedly commanded Ismail to remain at his post and continue serving.

In an extraordinary disclosure, the Negeri Sembilan palace confirmed that it had yet to verify the authenticity of the resignation letter, which was delivered to royal officials at 12.16am yesterday by an individual representing a private law firm.

The palace stressed that under the state constitution, the menteri besar is required to tender his resignation directly to the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, with any relinquishment of office taking legal effect only upon receiving the consent of the Ruler.

The irregular delivery and sudden public announcement have drawn intense scrutiny across the state, prompting questions over whether the coalition leadership overstepped constitutional propriety by preempting the palace.

Title: AG and FT minister fought Najib’s conditional pardon, leaked Pardons Board minutes show
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh both registered firm objections to granting former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon for house arrest during the Sept 18 Pardons Board meeting, according to purported minutes of the confidential session leaked online.

Excerpts of the document surfaced on the social media page of a former DAP lawmaker detailing high-level deliberations over the controversial royal clemency order.

The authenticity of the uploaded papers has not been independently verified by Malay Mail.

According to the leaked transcript, the attorney-general maintained his consistent stance that Najib should remain incarcerated in prison until 2028. Dusuki reportedly argued that house arrest is wholly absent from statutory legislation and remains “foreign” to the Malaysian legal system, citing a judicial precedent set by High Court Judge Alice Loke.

He cautioned that sanctioning home detention would trigger severe domestic and international repercussions, particularly harming political stability, the national economy, foreign investment, and Malaysia’s international standing, firmly insisting that Najib “should continue serving his sentence”.

The minister in the Prime Minister’s Department overseeing Federal Territories, an executive portfolio held by Yeoh, endorsed the attorney-general’s dissenting position, reaffirming her prior opposition to the pardon.

Although the minutes do not explicitly identify Yeoh by name, the record notes that after the board examined the draft terms of the home detention arrangement, both she and the attorney-general declined to provide feedback “given that they disagree with the conditional pardon”.

Despite their pushback, the minutes indicate that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, who chairs the Federal Territories Pardons Board under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution, was “inclined” to grant the conditional pardon, permitting Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest upon settling an RM50 million fine.

The document also details a procedural dispute over who should formally sign the release instrument. Pointing to counterfeit pardon orders circulating on social media and citing Section 14 of the Representation of Powers Act 1956, the minister suggested delegating the signature to an alternative official, such as the Cabinet secretary, given the acute political sensitivities involved.

While the AG requested time to evaluate the statutory provision, an officer on special duties to the King argued that it was inappropriate for the Chief Secretary to the Government to execute the document as he did not attend the meeting, with the monarch affirming that the civil service head is not a board member.

Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain cautioned that appointing an alternate signatory would provoke wider controversy by creating the impression that the minister had boycotted the proceedings. The King subsequently ruled that Yeoh must sign the order as the minister responsible for Federal Territories administration.

The leak arrives amid an escalating push within government for official disclosure. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail informed Parliament on Nov 12 that he would propose declassifying the minutes to the Cabinet, while Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil confirmed that ministers have sought formal legal counsel from the attorney-general.

Najib was transferred to his private residence earlier this month to begin serving his house arrest, which runs until August 2028.

Title: Sabah Immigration busts nomadic online fraud syndicate in Kota Kinabalu
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 18 — Twelve Chinese nationals operating a cross-border online financial scam syndicate from a residential bungalow in Damai have been arrested by immigration enforcement officers, the Sabah Immigration Department confirmed today.

The suspects, aged between 20 and 43, were apprehended during an 11.00am raid yesterday under Ops Serkap, mounted following intelligence surveillance and public tip-offs regarding suspicious activities at the upscale suburban property.

“During the operation, JIM Sabah seized 153 mobile phones of various models, 11 computers, one central processing unit (CPU), a printer, 13 routers, seven chargers, 22 SIM cards and three passports,” said Sabah Immigration director Datuk SH Sitti Saleha Habib Yussof during a Press conference today. Enforcement teams also confiscated assorted foreign currencies scattered across the premises.

Sitti Saleha said technical checks on the seized workstations revealed active ledgers linked to illicit financial fraud, though syndicate operators had hastily locked and signed out of most terminals as officers breached the perimeter.

“Only one computer was still active, allowing our team to examine the transactions carried out.

“One payment of about US$952 was detected, while other transactions ranged between US$950 and US$1,500,” she told a press conference at the department's headquarters here today.

Preliminary investigations indicate that the syndicate ran financial fraud schemes targeting victims across China, India, Cambodia, and Vietnam, with Sitti Saleha clarifying that the syndicate specialized in investment and financial swindles rather than romance scams. She noted that the syndicate operated nomadically, abandoning rental properties the moment they suspected law enforcement surveillance.

“Once they realise they are under surveillance, they move to another location. This makes it necessary for our intelligence team to continue tracking their movements,” she said.

Of the 12 suspects, four were found to have overstayed their visas by approximately two months and breached their pass conditions, while the remaining eight failed to produce valid travel documentation. The four who later presented passports are being investigated under Sections 51C and 39B of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while the undocumented eight face investigation under Section 61C. The department is also pursuing the property owner and local facilitators for harbouring undocumented migrants and unlawfully employing foreign workers.

In a related enforcement action, Sitti Saleha disclosed that two Chinese nationals were arrested on Nov 5 for running an unlicensed street vending operation at the weekly tamu market in Keningau. Investigators found that one individual held an expatriate pass as a construction engineer, while the other entered on a standard social visit tourist visa, with both caught retailing imported goods on ground mats.

Issuing a stern warning to employers and agents against allowing foreign nationals to undertake employment outside the authorised scope of their permits, Sitti Saleha reiterated that withholding foreign workers’ passports is strictly illegal. She added that while tourists are granted a standard 30-day stay, extension applications face rigorous scrutiny, with medical concessions generally capped at three days solely to allow visitors to make arrangements for their immediate repatriation.

Title: Ten former Negeri Sembilan exco members withdraw constitutional crisis suit
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 18 — The High Court here was informed today that 10 former Negeri Sembilan state executive council (Exco) members have withdrawn their originating summons against the State Secretary and two other parties over the constitutional crisis in the state, without liberty to file afresh.

High Court Judge Roz Mawar Rozain allowed the withdrawal after being informed by the plaintiffs’ counsel, Datuk Mohd Hafarizam Harun, that his clients had decided to withdraw the entire suit, including the application under the Federal Court’s original jurisdiction.

Hafarizam said the decision was made in view of recent developments concerning the resignation of Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, taking into account the constitutional provision that the entire state Exco would also cease to hold office when a Menteri Besar resigns.

“The reason for the withdrawal is that things have been overtaken by events, and that the Exco, in line with the constitutional provision that when a Menteri Besar resigns, the entire Exco will also fall or dissolve,” he said during the proceedings here today.

However, Roz Mawar pointed out that Ismail had not formally resigned at the time of the hearing, noting that he had only tendered his resignation letter and that approval from the Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir had yet to be received.

Hafarizam replied that the plaintiffs had initially sought an adjournment until Friday to allow time for Tuanku Muhriz to issue a decree on the resignation, but after consulting their clients, they decided to withdraw the proceedings.

The court also ordered the plaintiffs to pay costs of RM20,000 to the first defendant, the State Secretary; RM20,000 to the second defendant, the State Government; and RM8,000 to the third defendant, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU), subject to allocator.

In her remarks, Roz Mawar said the court would not discourage any litigant from withdrawing legal proceedings, adding that it could be the more prudent course of action.

However, she noted that the court had devoted considerable time and resources to the case since the originating summons was filed five months ago under a certificate of urgency, including dealing with various applications and setting timelines for the hearing of preliminary objections.

She said parties invoking the court’s jurisdiction, particularly on an urgent basis involving constitutional questions concerning the state government, also bore a responsibility towards the use of judicial resources, which were held in trust for the public.

Earlier, Hafarizam also informed the court that the withdrawal was made without liberty to file afresh, including by way of judicial review.

Counsel for the first defendant Datuk Dr Cyrus Das and counsel for the second defendant Razlan Hadri Zulkifli confirmed their consent to the withdrawal on the agreed terms, while counsel for the third defendant Steven Thiru also adopted the same position.

The 10 former Exco members had filed the lawsuit seeking an interpretation of the State Constitution and named the State Secretary and the State Government as defendants, while DKU was granted leave to intervene in the suit.

The plaintiffs were also represented by counsels Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun, Datuk Syed Faisal Al-Edros Syed Abdullah, Norhazira Abu Haiyan and Muhammad Luqman Hakeem Abas, while the first defendant was also represented by Abdul Rashid Ismail, Siti Nurani Md Zahidi and Diong Pei Jing.

Counsels Razlan Hadri Zulkifli, Marisa Regina Mohd Aris Rizal and Muhammad Yazid Mohamad Salim acted for the state government, while DKU was represented by Steven Thiru, David Mathew, Shafrin Halim and Gurjeevan Singh. — Bernama

Title: Data centre boom powers Malaysia’s Q3 GDP to 5.5pc expansion, DOSM says
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 18 — Malaysia’s multi-billion-ringgit data centre boom has transitioned from an investment narrative into a measurable macroeconomic force, emerging as a core engine that lifted non-residential construction, digital services, electronics manufacturing, and capital formation in the third quarter of 2026.

The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) reported today that gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 5.5 per cent year-on-year in the July-to-September period, moderating slightly from the 6.0 per cent pace recorded in the second quarter.

While overall growth eased, the statistics agency specifically highlighted data centre activities as an indispensable catalyst underpinning expansion across several high-performing industrial sub-sectors.

The physical buildout of computing infrastructure was most pronounced in the construction sector, which advanced 5.9 per cent on the back of a 16.7 per cent surge in non-residential civil engineering and building projects.

DOSM confirmed that heavy structural outlays for hyperscale server facilities drove the expansion, far outpacing specialized construction activities at 6.6 per cent. In the services domain, the information and communication sub-sector registered an 8.7 per cent jump, outperforming all other service segments on the back of rising server hosting, software management, and commercial data operations.

The technology spillover also reinforced high-value manufacturing, which expanded 7.7 per cent. Within the sector, the electrical, electronic, and optical products segment jumped 16.5 per cent, propelled by sustained global appetite for semiconductors, telecommunications hardware, and electronic components.

Concurrently, corporate investment gathered aggressive momentum. Gross fixed capital formation (GFCF), which measures spending on productive physical assets, climbed 8.1 per cent, nearly doubling the 4.6 per cent registered in the second quarter. The acceleration was powered by a 12.7 per cent jump in machinery and equipment procurement alongside a 5.5 per cent rise in structural investments, with DOSM crediting private sector industrial commitments for leading the charge.

The third-quarter figures lift economic expansion across the first nine months of the year to 5.6 per cent, up from 4.8 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025, while the economy posted a 1.5 per cent seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter expansion.

Household spending remained a foundational pillar of stability, with private consumption, which comprises 60.6 per cent of national output, rising 4.3 per cent, supported by double-digit gains of 10.4 per cent in restaurants and hotels and a 7.0 per cent increase in transport spending.

However, drag from extractive and public-sector outlays tempered top-line results. The mining and quarrying sector contracted 6.1 per cent, weighed down by a 12.4 per cent drop in crude oil and condensate extraction, while federal government spending slowed sharply to 1.2 per cent from 7.6 per cent in the prior quarter amid lower procurement expenditures.

Offsetting those contractions, the agriculture sector rebounded to 1.4 per cent growth after shrinking 3.6 per cent in the second quarter.

Title: Lim Guan Eng questions RM210m annual Perak water payment, warns Penang tariffs could surge past RM7
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 18 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has launched a scathing critique of Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow and state exco member Zairil Khir Johari, accusing the state leadership of disappointing residents by refusing to justify a 40-year water pact that requires Penang to pay Perak RM210 million annually, even if zero treated water is delivered.

In a statement today, the former Penang chief minister revealed that the total financial exposure under the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme amounts to at least RM24.6 billion over four decades beginning March 31, 2032.

The mammoth commitment comprises RM8.4 billion in fixed capacity charges and an estimated RM16.2 billion in variable volumetric supply charges.

“This shocking revelation of PBAPP, a PBAH wholly-owned subsidiary, paying a mandatory RM 210 million annually despite getting nothing in return was exposed by 5 independent directors at PBA Holdings Bhd(PBAH) Extraordinary General Meeting on 12.11.2026,” he said.

The contentious deal triggered internal dissent within the board of PBA Holdings Bhd (PBAH), the listed parent entity of state water operator Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang (PBAPP). Five of PBAH’s 12 directors, whom Lim described as seasoned and experienced professionals, formally recorded their objections to the off-take agreement during an extraordinary general meeting on Nov 12.

The dissenting bloc, comprising Datuk Brian Tan Guan Hooi, Lim Eng Huat, Nor Hatina Md Salleh, Lim Seang Lee, and Raja Azmi Raja Nazuddin, raised serious alarms that PBAPP remains contractually saddled with the RM210 million annual capacity levy regardless of whether Perak delivers the contracted 300 million litres of treated water daily, or supplies nothing at all.

Beyond the fixed RM8.4 billion commitment, Lim cautioned that escalating supply charges could trigger punishing tariff hikes for Penang domestic and industrial consumers. While the opening base tariff is set at RM1.70 per cubic metre, contractual escalations project the rate to rise to RM7.21 per cubic metre across the concession timeline. End-user tariffs could absorb an additional RM1 per cubic metre to cover internal operational costs, with rates potentially surging beyond the RM7.21 ceiling following a scheduled contract review after 22 years.

Lim noted that while steep consumption tariffs could be contested on pricing merits, “at least we are paying for something” physically received.

The core defect of the transaction, he argued, is an unconditional capacity penalty that leaves Penang taxpayers liable to pay hundreds of millions annually for non-existent water.

Condemning the state administration for compromising public interest through an unbalanced commercial framework, Lim demanded full transparency from the chief minister.

“This is an unequal agreement to the people of Penang that is irrational, contrary to sound logic and opposite to not only good governance but also responsible leadership,” Lim said.

He warned that refusing to account for the lopsided arrangement will severely undermine public confidence in the state administration as the staggering financial liability becomes widely understood across Penang.

Title: Two dead, one injured after Honda Civic crashes with poultry truck on Gerik-Jeli Highway
Article:
IPOH, Nov 18 — Two people were killed and another injured when the car they were travelling in collided with a lorry transporting chickens on the East-West Highway (JRTB) between Gerik and Jeli, near Gerik, early this morning.

Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call at 12.52 am, prompting the dispatch of personnel from the Gerik Fire and Rescue Station, located about 60 kilometres from the scene.

The team arrived at the scene at 1.55 am.

He identified the deceased as Razali Shakri, 45, and Normalizah Abd Manap, 36. Both were pronounced dead at the scene by Ministry of Health (KKM) personnel, and their bodies were handed over to the police.

He said another woman travelling in the Honda Civic sustained injuries, while the driver and attendant of the Isuzu lorry escaped unhurt.

“The operations commander conducted an initial assessment of the scene and adopted the SAVER (Systematic Approach for Victim Extrication and Rescue) concept. Personnel then carried out rescue operations using specialised equipment and a stretcher to extricate the victims.

“The injured woman was handed over to KKM personnel and taken to hospital by ambulance,” he said in a statement today.

Sabarodzi said the operation was brought under control at 2.35 am, and fully concluded at 3.40 am. — Bernama

Title: Police shoot dead robbery suspect linked to 24 cases in Chow Kit hotel raid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — A wanted criminal linked to at least 24 robberies across the capital was shot dead after opening fire on a joint police strike team during a pre-dawn raid on a hotel in Chow Kit today.

The operation unfolded around 2.00am when detectives from the Special Investigation Division (D9) of the Kuala Lumpur police contingent, supported by Bukit Aman personnel, tracked down the suspect's hideout and breached the hotel room, Berita Harian reported.

Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the armed suspect resisted arrest and immediately discharged his weapon towards the entry team.

“The suspect fired several shots at the police during the raid, forcing officers to return fire in self-defence.

“The exchange of gunfire continued until the security threat was successfully neutralised,” he told the media at the scene today.

Attending medical personnel pronounced the local suspect dead at the scene.

“Police also seized a firearm and drugs suspected to be methamphetamine, which were found in the suspect’s room.

“Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect, who had nine previous criminal records, was wanted by police and used a modus operandi of posing as a taxi driver to rob passengers, particularly women and senior citizens,” he said.

Fadil noted that the operation effectively resolved 24 unsolved street robbery cases that had targeted vulnerable commuters across the city.

The case is being investigated under Sections 392 and 397 of the Penal Code for armed robbery, with detectives pursuing follow-up operations to track down remaining accomplices tied to the criminal network.

Title: Zahid says he ‘believes’ decision was made after Ismail Lasim’s royal audience last night, palace to announce outcome
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Nov 18 — All decisions and official announcements regarding the resignation status of Datuk Ismail Lasim and the candidate for the new Menteri Besar will be left entirely to the discretion of the Negeri Sembilan Palacesaid Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

Ahmad Zahid, who is also Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said further details on the matter would have to await an announcement by the palace.

“Let the outcome be announced by the palace itself and Datuk Ismail Lasim. So, I believe that something has been jointly decided by the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir and Datuk Ismail (during yesterday’s audience),” he said.

He was speaking at a press conference after chairing the Coordination Meeting between the Deputy Prime Minister-cum-Rural and Regional Development Minister and Rural Development Excos (MEXCLUB) at the Desaru Coast Conference Centre here today.

Commenting further, Ahmad Zahid said he had sent a letter to the palace but had yet to receive any royal summons for an audience.

“A letter has been sent. So far, I have not received any royal summons for an audience, and we have confidence in the state leadership to present the letter for consideration. There is only one name, but let the palace make the announcement,” he said.

Last Monday, Ismail, 67, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, was reported to have resigned as Menteri Besar. He was sworn in as Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar on August 2.

Meanwhile, Ahmad Zahid stressed that the resignation of the Menteri Besar was an official state administrative matter and should not be conflated with personal or family matters.

Yesterday, the Negeri Sembilan Palace said the Menteri Besar’s resignation would only take effect after obtaining the consent of Tuanku Muhriz, in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan.

Tuanku Muhriz was also reported to have granted an audience to Ismail yesterday following the current political impasse in the state. The audience began at about 5pm and ended at 6.30pm.

Last Monday, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said Ahmad Zahid, who is also UMNO president, had received a copy of the resignation letter, which had been sent to Tuanku Muhriz.

In the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election (PRN), BN won 18 State Legislative Assembly (DUN) seats while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven, enabling the two coalitions to form the state government with a two-thirds majority. — Bernama
